247	<Shot
248	  name="04b-preview-scopes.preview"
249	  alt="The Waveform in the top slot of the Scopes panel beside the preview: a dark panel labelled 0, 50 and 100 at its left, with a white trace, red marks along its top and bottom edges, and under it the readouts Highlights clipped 1.9 % and Shadows clipped 52.7 %."
250	/>
251	
252	To see them, press <kbd>⌃⌘W</kbd> to open the [Scopes](/color/scopes/) panel, then choose **Waveform** or **Parade** from a slot's popup. A new window's top slot is already on **Waveform**. Each takes 200 pt of height when the pane has room, and [shrinks to fit](/color/scopes/#when-the-pane-is-short) when it doesn't.
253	
254	In an HDR project they read differently, and [Scopes in an HDR project](/hdr/hdr-scopes/) has the scale.
255	
256	## Read the waveform
257	
258	The Waveform plots the picture's luma (Y′, its brightness). Left to right in the scope is left to right across the frame, and height is brightness, with black at the bottom and white at the top. So a bright window on the left of the shot shows as a high patch on the left of the scope.
259	
260	Lines mark 0, 25, 50, 75 and 100 %, with 0, 50 and 100 labelled at the left. The trace is white on a near-black background in both light and dark appearance. The brighter a point in the trace, the more pixels sit there, on a log scale, so a level only a few pixels reach still shows.
261	
262	## Read the RGB parade
263	
264	The Parade shows red, green and blue as three waveforms side by side, in that order, each tinted its own colour. Each one works like the Waveform, with the same lines and the whole width of the frame.
265	
266	Use it to see a colour cast. Something that should be neutral grey sits at the same height in all three, and a channel sitting higher or lower is pulling the picture toward or away from that colour. **Temperature** and **Tint** in [Light](/color/light/), and the [wheels](/color/wheels/), are the usual ways to bring them back in line.
267	
268	## Find clipping
269	
270	A pixel clips high at the top level, where an 8-bit file would write 255, and low at the bottom level, where it would write 0. Detail at those levels has gone flat.
271	
272	**Clip marks** are red marks on the top and bottom edges of the scope. A mark sits over every column where at least 0.5 % of the pixels clip, on the top edge for highlights and the bottom edge for shadows, so you can see where in the frame it's happening. The Parade marks each channel on its own, so one channel can clip when the others don't.
273	
274	**Readouts** under the Waveform give the share of the whole frame, for example **Highlights clipped 1.9 %** and **Shadows clipped 52.7 %**. They show "—" until a frame has been measured. The [Histogram](/color/histogram/) has the same two readouts. The Parade and the Vectorscope have none.
275	
276	The readouts count everything in the frame. A black background around a smaller clip counts as clipped shadows, so a high figure may not be a problem with your footage. To bring highlights down, try **Exposure** or **Highlights** in [Light](/color/light/).
277	
278	## With an agent
279	
280	`render_frame` measures a frame's Waveform or Parade without the panel. Pass `waveform` or `parade` as true. Both are false by default. The tool's reply says what share of pixels clips high and low, and for the Parade it gives that for each channel, which the panel doesn't show as a number.
281	
282	A JSON file next to the image holds the raw counts, in 256 × 256 bins, with the clip marks and the clipping figures. It's named `<image path>.waveform.json` or `<image path>.parade.json`, and the Parade's holds red, green and blue separately. See [Check the picture: render_frame](/mcp/render-frame/#waveform-parade-and-histogram).

296	import { Steps } from '@astrojs/starlight/components';
297	import AtAGlance from '@components/AtAGlance.astro';

299	
300	The vectorscope shows a frame's colour with its brightness taken away: which hues are in the picture and how strong they are. Use it to spot a colour cast, to check skin tones, and to see how far a grade has pushed saturation.
301	
302	<AtAGlance
303	  menu="View ▸ Scopes"
304	  keys="⌃⌘W"
305	  where="The Scopes panel ▸ a slot's popup ▸ Vectorscope"
306	  tools="render_frame"

309	<Shot
310	  name="04b-preview-scopes.preview"
311	  alt="The preview with the Scopes panel beside it. The bottom slot shows the Vectorscope, a near-black square with six labelled target boxes around it, R at the top, Mg top right, B right, Cy at the bottom, G bottom left and Yl left. A line runs from the centre cross up and to the left, and a thin white trace runs from the centre towards the B box, for the blue card in the picture. The 1×, 2× and 4× cells sit in the bottom-right corner, with 1× filled."
312	/>
313	
314	## Open the vectorscope
315	
316	Choose **View ▸ Scopes**. In a new window the panel starts with **Waveform** on top and **Vectorscope** below. If a slot shows something else, pick **Vectorscope** from its popup. Both slots can show it, each at its own zoom. See [Scopes](/color/scopes/) for the panel itself.
317	
318	## Read the trace
319	
320	Every pixel in the frame lands somewhere on the near-black square, and the white trace is all of them together.
321	
322	- **The centre is no colour.** Greys, black and white all sit on the faint cross.
323	- **Distance from the centre is strength.** A pale colour stays close in, and a saturated one reaches out towards the edge.
324	- **Direction is hue.** The [targets](#the-targets) show which way each colour lies.
325	- **Brightness is how many pixels are there.** The scale is logarithmic, so a small patch of colour still shows up beside a large one.
326	
327	The two axes are the colour-difference signals: Cb runs across and Cr runs up. The scope draws no circles and has no readouts, so the targets and the skin line are your only references.
328	
329	A picture with no colour cast keeps its neutral areas on the cross. If something that should be grey sits to one side of it, the picture leans the way the trace leans. [Zoom in](#zoom-in-on-a-low-saturation-picture) to see a small cast.
330	
331	## The targets
332	
333	Six boxes mark where 75 % colour bars land, so you can tell which way a colour lies and how strong it is. Each label sits outside its box, away from the centre.
334	
335	| Label | Colour | Where it sits |
336	| --- | --- | --- |
337	| R | Red | Up, a little left |
338	| Mg | Magenta | Up and right |
339	| B | Blue | Right, a little down |
340	| Cy | Cyan | Down, a little right |
341	| G | Green | Down and left |
342	| Yl | Yellow | Left, a little up |
343	
344	## The skin line
345	
346	The line running out from the centre, up and to the left, marks where skin tones fall. It's drawn at the hue of a standard light-skin reference colour, 123.3° anticlockwise from the right.
347	
348	Skin has a similar hue across complexions, and mostly differs in brightness and strength. If the trace from a face sits well to one side of the line, the picture has a cast.
349	
350	## Zoom in on a low-saturation picture
351	
352	The **1×**, **2×** and **4×** cells in the scope's bottom-right corner zoom in around the centre, to show small casts in a picture with little colour in it. Click a cell to choose it. The filled cell is the current zoom.
353	
354	Frame Job counts the pixels again at each zoom instead of enlarging the picture of the trace, so a magnified trace stays sharp.
355	
356	At 2× and 4×, a pixel too strong to fit on the square is left off, and it isn't piled up against the edge. At 1× everything fits.
357	
358	All six targets are too far out to fit at 2× and 4×. Each one becomes a 6 pt tick on the rim that points towards it, with its label inside the rim.
359	
360	Each slot keeps its own zoom when you pick another scope and come back, and when you hide the panel and show it again. A zoom lasts while the window is open. It isn't saved, and every slot starts at 1× in a new window. A cell works on the first click, even when its window isn't the active one.
361	
362	## Good to know
363	
364	- The scope measures the frame the preview composes, so it follows playback, your edits and [Show Ungraded](/color/show-ungraded/). It changes nothing in the project or in an export.
365	- The slot's caption says what the scope reads: "Rec. 709 · encoded", the picture's own encoded values.
366	- In an HDR (HLG) project the caption reads "Rec. 2100 HLG", and the targets and the skin line are redrawn for that colour space, with the skin line at 139.9°. With **Show SDR Version** on, the scope reads that SDR picture as it would in an SDR project. See [Scopes in an HDR project](/hdr/hdr-scopes/).
367	- The scope is a 224 pt square. If the preview pane is too short for both slots, it shrinks with them and stays square. Under 360 pt tall, only the top slot shows.
368	
369	## With an agent
370	
371	`render_frame` measures a frame's vectorscope as numbers when an agent passes `vectorscope: true`, which is off by default. `vectorscope_zoom` chooses 1, 2 or 4, and is 1 unless set. The reply says what share of the frame is neutral and, at 2 and 4, what share lies off the plot. The counts, the targets and the skin line's angle go to a `.vectorscope.json` file beside the image. None of this changes a slot's zoom in the panel. See [Check the picture: render_frame](/mcp/render-frame/#vectorscope-and-vectorscope_zoom).

392	## Compare with the ungraded picture
393	
394	Press <kbd>⌃⌘U</kbd>, or choose **View ▸ Show Ungraded**. Press it again to go back to the graded picture. The menu item has a checkmark while it's on, and it's always available.
395	
396	While it's on, every clip's **Light**, **Color**, **Wheels**, **Curves** and **Look** are set to neutral in this window's preview and the [Preview Window](/timeline/preview-window/). That includes nested clips, clips in a [matte](/canvas/matte-tracks/) and [adjustment clips](/color/adjustment-clips/), so the grade an adjustment clip puts on everything behind it goes too.
397	
398	The project doesn't change. It isn't an edit, and it makes no undo step.
399	
400	[Scopes](/color/scopes/) read the preview's frame, so they follow the switch and measure the ungraded picture.
401	
402	## The Ungraded tag
403	
404	An **Ungraded** tag shows in the preview's top-left corner while the switch is on, so you can't mistake the plain picture for your grade. See [Preview tags](/timeline/preview/#preview-tags).
405	
406	## What it leaves on
407	
408	Show Ungraded only takes away the grade. These aren't part of the grade, so they stay on:
409	
410	- A [camera-log conversion](/hdr/camera-log/) on the media. It's how the file is read, so turning it off wouldn't give you the true source.
411	- [Filters](/effects/filters/).
412	- The [chroma key](/effects/chroma-key/).
413	- Placement, and everything else about a clip, such as its opacity and blend mode.
414	
415	## Grade view tools are never saved
416	
417	Show Ungraded, [Show Selection](/color/show-selection/) and the [scopes](/color/scopes/) only change how this window shows the picture. Each belongs to the window, each is off in a new window, and nothing about them is saved.
418	
419	None of them reaches an export or **Save Frame…**, which always use the graded picture. The thumbnails in the [Look](/color/looks/) gallery ignore Show Ungraded too.
420	
421	## With an agent
422	
423	Pass `ungraded: true` to `render_frame` to draw a frame as if no clip were graded. It's false by default, and the tool's reply says the frame has every grade removed. The tool works the same whether the View menu switch is on or off, and it leaves the switch alone. See [Check the picture: render_frame](/mcp/render-frame/#ungraded).
424

432	title: "Copy a grade"
433	description: "Give other clips the grade you built on one clip, what comes with it, how LUTs and qualifiers travel, and what stops a paste."
434	---
435	
436	import { Steps } from '@astrojs/starlight/components';
437	import AtAGlance from '@components/AtAGlance.astro';
438	
439	When one clip looks right, Paste Attributes gives its grade to any number of other clips in one undo step. This page covers what that means for a grade. [Paste Attributes](/editing/paste-attributes/) covers the command in full.
440	
441	<AtAGlance
442	  menu="Edit ▸ Paste Attributes"
443	  keys={['⌘C', '⌥⌘V']}
444	  tools={['paste_attributes', 'paste']}
445	/>
446	
447	## Copy a grade with Paste Attributes
448	
449	<Steps>
450	
451	1. Select the graded clip and press <kbd>⌘C</kbd>.
452	
453	2. Select the clips that should take the grade.
454	
455	3. Press <kbd>⌥⌘V</kbd>, or choose **Edit ▸ Paste Attributes**.
456	
457	</Steps>
458	
459	The copied clip's video settings replace each selected clip's, as one undo step called Paste Attributes. If nothing would change, Frame Job beeps.
460	
461	## What comes with the grade
462	
463	There's no way to paste the grade alone, because it travels with the rest of the clip's picture settings:
464	
465	- Light, Color, Wheels, Curves, and the look with its **Amount**
466	- filters
467	- everything else about the picture, including position and scale
468	- the audio settings too, where the copied clip has sound and the target can take them
469	
470	A clip's place, speed, actions, transitions, name and label never come across.
471	
472	:::caution
473	Position and scale come with the grade. Pasting onto a clip you've already placed moves it to where the copied clip sits. To share a grade without touching placement, put an [adjustment clip](/color/adjustment-clips/) above the clips instead.
474	:::
475	
476	The paste replaces, it doesn't merge, so anything the target had that the copied clip didn't is gone. A grade that lives in an [action](/color/animate-a-grade/) doesn't travel either, because actions stay behind. The target takes the copied clip's own values, not its animation.
477	
478	## LUTs travel with a paste
479	
480	A look that uses an imported [`.cube` LUT](/color/luts/) keeps working when you paste it into another project, with Paste Attributes or with **Edit ▸ Paste**. The LUT arrives in that project's media along with the clip, and if the project already has the same file, the paste uses that one.
481	
482	A pasted look never lands on the wrong file. If what's being pasted doesn't carry the LUT, the clip gets no look.
483	
484	## A qualifier between clips
485	
486	A [qualifier](/color/qualifiers/) belongs to an adjustment clip, so what happens to it depends on the clips at both ends of the paste.
487	
488	| Pasting | The qualifier |
489	| --- | --- |
490	| Onto a picture clip | Is dropped |
491	| From a picture clip onto an adjustment clip | Stays as the adjustment clip had it |
492	| From one adjustment clip onto another | Is copied |
493	
494	## When a paste stops
495	
496	An adjustment clip has no picture of its own, so some settings can't land on it. If the copied clip has a blur, sharpen or pixelate filter, or a blend mode, pasting onto an adjustment clip shows an error naming the clip and the setting, and nothing changes on any selected clip.
497	
498	Sepia, noir, vignette and invert filters paste onto an adjustment clip without trouble.
499	
500	To get past it, take the setting off the copied clip and copy it again, or leave the adjustment clip out of the selection. [When a paste stops](/editing/paste-attributes/#when-a-paste-stops) has the full list, for every kind of clip.
501	
502	## With an agent
503	
504	The menu item always copies each of the picture, sound, text and shape groups both clips have. An agent can list the ones it wants in `paste_attributes`'s `groups`, out of `video`, `audio`, `text`, `shape` and `graphic`, so `["video"]` brings the picture settings and leaves the sound alone. The grade is still part of `video`, so to set a grade and nothing else, an agent uses `set_video`. See [Tools: copying and nesting](/mcp/tools-copy-and-nest/#paste_attributes).
505

22	title: The Color tab
23	description: Find every grading control in one place, learn what can be graded and in what order a grade applies, and grade several clips at once.
24	---
25	
26	import { Steps } from '@astrojs/starlight/components';
27	import AtAGlance from '@components/AtAGlance.astro';
28	import Shot from '@components/Shot.astro';
29	
30	Grading is how you correct a clip's colour and tone and give it a look of its own. The **Color** sub-tab of the Clip tab holds every control for it: exposure and white balance, colour wheels, curves and looks. The settings on a clip are its grade.
31	
32	<AtAGlance
33	  where="Clip tab ▸ Color"
34	  tools={['set_video', 'set_action_end', 'undo']}
35	/>
36	
37	## Open the Color tab
38	
39	<Steps>
40	
41	1. Select one or more clips on the timeline.
42	
43	2. Open the inspector's **Clip** tab.
44	
45	3. Choose **Color** in the row of sub-tabs.
46	
47	4. Open the section you want by clicking its header.
48	
49	</Steps>
50	
51	<Shot
52	  name="05b-clip-color.window"
53	  alt="The editor window with a video clip selected. In the inspector on the right, the Clip tab's Color sub-tab is chosen and its Light section is open, showing nine sliders with number fields, all at zero. The Color and Wheels section headers sit below it, each reading neutral."
54	/>
55	
56	A video clip opens on **Picture**, so you choose **Color** yourself. Selecting a different clip sends the inspector back to that clip's first sub-tab. An adjustment clip has no **Picture** sub-tab, so it opens on **Color**.
57	
58	## What can be graded
59	
60	These clips can take a grade:
61	
62	- Video clips
63	- Image clips
64	- Stills (freeze frames)
65	- [Adjustment clips](/color/adjustment-clips/), which grade everything behind them
66	
67	Text, shape, graphic and nest clips have no **Color** sub-tab. Nor does a clip from an audio-only file.
68	
69	### Mixed selections
70	
71	The sub-tab shows only when everything selected can take a grade, with one exception for sound.
72	
73	| Selected together | What happens |
74	| --- | --- |
75	| A video clip and an audio-only clip | The sub-tab stays. The grade goes only to the clips with a picture. |
76	| A video clip and a text, shape, graphic or nest clip | The sub-tab goes. Deselect the text, shape, graphic or nest clip to get it back. |
77	| A video clip and an adjustment clip | The sub-tab stays, and **Picture** goes. The Adjustment and Qualifier sections don't show, because not every clip is an adjustment clip. |
78	
79	## The sections
80	
81	The sections run down the tab in this order.
82	
83	| Section | What it's for | Shown for |
84	| --- | --- | --- |
85	| **Adjustment** | How strongly an adjustment clip's grade applies. See [Adjustment clips](/color/adjustment-clips/). | Adjustment clips only |
86	| **Qualifier** | Narrowing an adjustment clip's grade to one colour or tone range. See [Qualifiers](/color/qualifiers/). | Adjustment clips only |
87	| **Light** | Exposure, white balance and tone. See [Light](/color/light/). | Every gradable clip |
88	| **Color** | Overall brightness, contrast, saturation and hue. See [Brightness, contrast, saturation and hue](/color/color-section/). | Every gradable clip |
89	| **Wheels** | Pushing the shadows, middle tones and highlights toward a colour. See [Wheels](/color/wheels/). | Every gradable clip |
90	| **Curves** | Shaping tones and hues with points on a curve. See [Master and RGB curves](/color/curves/) and [Hue vs Hue and Hue vs Sat curves](/color/hue-curves/). | Every gradable clip |
91	| **Look** | A built-in look or your own LUT. See [Looks](/color/looks/) and [.cube LUTs](/color/luts/). | Every gradable clip |
92	
93	Adjustment and Qualifier show only when every selected clip is an adjustment clip.
94	
95	### Which section opens
96	
97	Every section starts closed. If no section is open when the tab appears, it opens the first one you haven't closed yourself. Once you've opened or closed a section, Frame Job remembers that, for every clip and the next time you launch it.
98	
99	With an [action](/color/animate-a-grade/) selected, the sections it animates open by themselves. That doesn't change how you left them.
100	
101	### Read a section header
102	
103	A section's header sums up its state, so you can see what a clip carries without opening anything.
104	
105	| Section | The header reads |
106	| --- | --- |
107	| **Light**, **Color**, **Wheels**, **Curves** | "neutral" or "adjusted" |
108	| **Look** | "none", the look and its amount such as "Warm 80%", or "mixed" when the selected clips differ |
109	| **Qualifier** | "off", or what's on, such as "hue · sat · inverted" |
110	| **Adjustment** | The strength, such as "75%" |
111	
112	## Reset a section
113	
114	**Reset** appears in a section's header while the section differs from its default. It returns that section to neutral and touches nothing else, so resetting Light leaves Color alone. On Adjustment it puts **Strength** back to 100 %.
115	
116	To put back one control rather than a whole section, right-click its label or slider and choose **Reset to default**. It's dimmed while the row already holds its default.
117	
118	With an action selected, a section doesn't offer **Reset**. It shows **Clear** instead while the action animates any of that section's rows, and **Clear** takes the section out of the action. On a row, the right-click item reads **Set end value to default**. See [Animate a grade](/color/animate-a-grade/).
119	
120	## Grade several clips at once
121	
122	Select the clips and use the tab as you would for one. A control changes only its own value on each clip and keeps their other values, so dragging **Exposure** across three clips changes their exposure and nothing else.
123	
124	The value you set is the same on every clip. It isn't an offset from what each clip had.
125	
126	When the selected clips hold different values for a control, its row shows a **mixed** badge.
127	
128	An action belongs to one clip, so with several clips selected every control sets the clips' own values, even if one of them has an action.
129	
130	## Undo in the Color tab
131	
132	| You did this | It's one undo step named |
133	| --- | --- |
134	| Dragged a slider or typed a value | The control: **Undo Exposure**, **Undo Hue**, **Undo Strength** |
135	| Pressed a section's **Reset** | The section: **Undo Light**, **Undo Color**, **Undo Wheels**, **Undo Curves**, **Undo Look**, **Undo Adjustment**, **Undo Qualifier** |
136	| Pressed a section's **Clear** | **Undo Clear** |
137	
138	## The fixed grade order
139	
140	A grade always applies in one order, whatever order you made the changes in:
141	
142	1. **Color**: brightness, contrast, saturation and hue.
143	2. **Light**.
144	3. **Wheels**.
145	4. **Curves**: the tone curves first, then the hue curves.
146	5. **Look**.
147	
148	You can't change this order, so the same settings always give the same picture. The tab lists Light above Color, but Color acts first.
149	
150	A [Camera Log](/hdr/camera-log/) conversion set on the media comes before all of these, and a [chroma key](/effects/chroma-key/) follows it, so a key reads the picture before your grade.
151	
152	## Filters around the grade
153	
154	The [filters](/effects/filters/) in the Picture sub-tab act on either side of the grade, which matters when you combine one with a grade.
155	
156	| Filter | Where it acts |
157	| --- | --- |
158	| Pixelate | Before the grade |
159	| Blur, Sharpen | After Color's four controls and before Light |
160	| Sepia, Noir, Vignette, Invert | After the Look, in the order you [stacked them](/effects/filters/#stack-and-reorder-filters) |
161	
162	So a filter such as Noir or Vignette works on the graded colour.
163	
164	[Show Ungraded](/color/show-ungraded/) leaves filters on, because they aren't part of the grade.
165	
166	## One grade everywhere
167	
168	The preview, **File ▸ Save Frame…** and every export apply a grade the same way, so what you see while grading is what you get.
169	
170	A clip you haven't graded renders exactly as it would without a grade. A neutral section does nothing to the picture.
171

182	title: Brightness, contrast, saturation and hue
183	description: Make overall changes to a clip's picture with the Color section's Brightness, Contrast, Saturation and Hue controls.
184	---
185	
186	import { Steps } from '@astrojs/starlight/components';
187	import AtAGlance from '@components/AtAGlance.astro';
188	
189	The Color section makes broad changes to the whole picture: brighter, punchier, more or less colourful, or every colour turned around the wheel.
190	
191	<AtAGlance
192	  where="Clip tab ▸ Color ▸ Color"
193	  tools={['set_video', 'set_action_end']}
194	/>
195	
196	## The Color section
197	
198	<Steps>
199	
200	1. Select the clip and open the [**Color**](/color/color-tab/) sub-tab.
201	
202	2. Open the **Color** section by clicking its header. It starts closed.
203	
204	3. Drag a slider, or type in the number field beside it.
205	
206	</Steps>
207	
208	All four controls start at 0.
209	
210	| Control | Range | Shows | What it does |
211	| --- | --- | --- | --- |
212	| **Brightness** | −1 to +1 | Two decimals | Raises or lowers every level |
213	| **Contrast** | −1 to +1 | Two decimals | Spreads the tones apart or pulls them together |
214	| **Saturation** | −1 to +1 | Two decimals | More or less colour overall |
215	| **Hue** | −180° to +180° | Whole degrees | Turns every colour around the colour wheel |
216	
217	**Reset** in the header clears these four as one undo step, **Undo Color**, and leaves [Light](/color/light/) alone. The header reads "neutral" or "adjusted".
218	
219	With an [action](/color/animate-a-grade/) selected, every control here sets the value the action animates to, rather than the clip's own value.
220	
221	## Brightness
222	
223	**Brightness** adds the same amount to every level, so the blacks rise or fall with everything else. Use it for an overall lift of the whole picture. Frame Job has no Offset wheel, so this is the control for that job.
224	
225	To brighten the way a camera would, with black staying black, use [Exposure](/color/light/#set-the-exposure).
226	
227	## Contrast
228	
229	**Contrast** spreads the tones away from the middle or pulls them toward it. At +1 the spread doubles. At −1 every tone meets at mid-grey.
230	
231	For finer control over which tones move, use [the curves](/color/curves/).
232	
233	## Saturation
234	
235	**Saturation** gives more or less colour across the whole picture. −1 is greyscale and +1 is twice the colour.
236	
237	It moves every colour alike. To favour the muted colours and spare the strong ones, use [Vibrance](/color/light/#add-colour-with-vibrance).
238	
239	## Hue
240	
241	**Hue** turns every colour around the colour wheel by the same angle, from −180° to +180°. Its field shows whole degrees. Positive turns red toward yellow and then green.
242	
243	Each pixel's brightness is kept, and greys stay grey.
244	
245	To turn one colour and leave the others alone, use [Hue vs Hue](/color/hue-curves/).
246	
247	## With an agent
248	
249	An agent sets these four in `set_video`'s `color` object, as `brightness`, `contrast`, `saturation` and `hue`, and `set_action_end` takes the same keys for an action. Any it doesn't name keep their values, and 0 means no change.
250	
251	An agent isn't held to the sliders' ranges for these four controls. `set_video` takes any finite number for them, with `hue` in degrees. [Light's controls](/color/light/#with-an-agent) are different: `set_video` won't take a value outside their ranges. See [Tools: picture and grade](/mcp/tools-set-video/#color).
252	
253	## Good to know
254	
255	- A number you type outside a control's range is pulled back to the nearest limit.
256	- These four act first in the grade, before Light, even though the tab lists Light above them. See [The fixed grade order](/color/color-tab/#the-fixed-grade-order).
257	- A [chroma key](/effects/chroma-key/) reads the picture before these controls, so changing them doesn't move the key.
258	- Blur and Sharpen act after these four. See [Filters around the grade](/color/color-tab/#filters-around-the-grade).
259	- On an [adjustment clip](/color/adjustment-clips/), these controls grade everything behind the clip.
260

269	title: Light
270	description: Correct a clip's exposure and white balance, and shape its highlights, shadows, black and white points, vibrance and fade.
271	---
272	
273	import { Steps } from '@astrojs/starlight/components';
274	import AtAGlance from '@components/AtAGlance.astro';
275	import Shot from '@components/Shot.astro';
276	
277	The Light section corrects how bright a clip is and how warm it looks, then shapes its tones. It's usually where a grade starts.
278	
279	<AtAGlance
280	  where="Clip tab ▸ Color ▸ Light"
281	  tools={['set_video', 'set_action_end']}
282	/>
283	
284	## The Light section
285	
286	<Steps>
287	
288	1. Select the clip and open the [**Color**](/color/color-tab/) sub-tab.
289	
290	2. Open the **Light** section by clicking its header, if it isn't open already.
291	
292	3. Drag a slider, or type in the number field beside it.
293	
294	</Steps>
295	
296	<Shot
297	  name="05b-clip-color.inspector"
298	  alt="The Color sub-tab with the Light section open. Nine rows run down it, Exposure, Temperature, Tint, Highlights, Shadows, Whites, Blacks, Vibrance and Fade, each a slider with a number field reading 0.00. Exposure's field shows EV, and Fade's slider sits at its left end while the others sit in the middle."
299	/>
300	
301	All nine controls start at 0, and each shows two decimals. The rows run in the order they act on the picture, so working down the list is a natural way to correct a clip.
302	
303	| Control | Range | What it does |
304	| --- | --- | --- |
305	| **Exposure** | −3 to +3 EV | Brightens or darkens in stops |
306	| **Temperature** | −1 to +1 | Warmer or cooler |
307	| **Tint** | −1 to +1 | Toward magenta or green |
308	| **Highlights** | −1 to +1 | Lifts or lowers the brighter half of the tones |
309	| **Shadows** | −1 to +1 | Lifts or lowers the darker half of the tones |
310	| **Whites** | −1 to +1 | Stretches the tones toward white, with black held |
311	| **Blacks** | −1 to +1 | Raises or deepens the dark end, with white held |
312	| **Vibrance** | −1 to +1 | Changes saturation mostly in colours that have little of it |
313	| **Fade** | 0 to 1 | Lifts black and lowers white, for a washed-out film look |
314	
315	**Reset** in the header sets all nine back to 0 as one undo step, **Undo Light**, and leaves the [Color section](/color/color-section/) alone. The header reads "neutral" or "adjusted".
316	
317	With an [action](/color/animate-a-grade/) selected, every control here sets the value the action animates to, rather than the clip's own value.
318	
319	## Set the exposure
320	
321	**Exposure** brightens or darkens the picture in stops, from −3 to +3 EV. +1 doubles the light and −1 halves it.
322	
323	It works on linear light, meaning the amount of light in the scene rather than the encoded picture values, the way a camera's exposure does. So black stays black. To lift every level by the same amount, black included, use [Brightness](/color/color-section/#brightness).
324	
325	To judge exposure by measurement rather than by eye, watch the [waveform](/color/waveform-and-parade/) as you drag.
326	
327	## Set the white balance
328	
329	**Temperature** and **Tint** work on linear light, like Exposure. Both run from −1 to +1.
330	
331	| Control | Positive | Negative | At the limit |
332	| --- | --- | --- | --- |
333	| **Temperature** | Warmer: more red, less blue | Cooler: more blue, less red | At +1 red rises and blue falls by 0.3 of a stop. −1 is the reverse. |
334	| **Tint** | Toward magenta | Toward green | At +1 green falls by 0.3 of a stop, which reads as magenta. −1 raises it. |
335	
336	## Lift or lower the highlights and shadows
337	
338	**Highlights** moves the brighter half of the tones and **Shadows** the darker half. Both run from −1 to +1, and neither touches the other's half.
339	
340	At ±1 each moves its tones by up to a quarter of the full range. The move is strongest at the extreme, white for Highlights and black for Shadows, and fades to nothing at the middle of the tonal range.
341	
342	## Set the white and black points
343	
344	**Whites** stretches the tones toward white and holds black where it is. **Blacks** does the same at the other end: positive raises the dark end, negative deepens it, and white is held. Both run from −1 to +1.
345	
346	Each is a stretch of up to 15 %.
347	
348	## Add colour with Vibrance
349	
350	**Vibrance** changes saturation mostly in colours that have little of it, from −1 to +1. Colours that are already strong are left mostly alone, which is the difference from [Saturation](/color/color-section/#saturation), which moves every colour alike.
351	
352	At +1 a nearly grey colour gets about twice its saturation, and at −1 it goes grey. A fully saturated colour doesn't change at either end.
353	
354	## Fade the picture
355	
356	**Fade** lifts black and lowers white for a washed-out film look. It runs from 0 to 1 and has no negative side. At 1, black rises to 10 % and white falls to 95 %.
357	
358	## With an agent
359	
360	One `set_video` call can set any of the nine Light controls and the four [Color](/color/color-section/) controls together, in its `color` object, and it leaves the ones it doesn't name alone. Each key is its control's name in lower case, such as `exposure` or `fade`, and 0 means no change. A positive `temperature` is warmer and a positive `tint` is more magenta. `set_action_end` takes the same keys for an action.
361	
362	A `set_video` call with a value outside a Light control's range fails, rather than being pulled back to the limit as a typed number is. `set_action_end` does take such a value, and the action stops at the limit when it's drawn. See [Tools: picture and grade](/mcp/tools-set-video/#color).
363	
364	## Good to know
365	
366	- A number you type outside a control's range is pulled back to the nearest limit.
367	- Light acts after the Color section's four controls, even though the tab lists it first. See [The fixed grade order](/color/color-tab/#the-fixed-grade-order).
368	- On an [adjustment clip](/color/adjustment-clips/), Light grades everything behind the clip.
369	- In an [HDR project](/hdr/dynamic-range/), Exposure works on the scene's light as HLG encodes it, so +1 still doubles the light.
370

382	---
383	
384	import { Steps } from '@astrojs/starlight/components';
385	import AtAGlance from '@components/AtAGlance.astro';

388	The wheels balance a picture by tone. **Lift** works on the shadows, **Gamma** on the middle tones and **Gain** on the highlights, so you can cool the shadows, warm the highlights or take a colour cast out of one part of the picture.
389

401	## The Wheels section
402	
403	<Steps>
404	
405	1. Select a video clip, an image, a still or an [adjustment clip](/color/adjustment-clips/). An adjustment clip's wheels grade everything behind it.
406	
407	2. Open the **Color** sub-tab of the Clip tab. See [The Color tab](/color/color-tab/) for which clips have it.
408	
409	3. Open **Wheels**. It starts closed, and its header reads **neutral** until a wheel moves, then **adjusted**.
410	
411	</Steps>
412	
413	Each of the three columns has a colour disc that [pushes its range toward a colour](#push-a-range-toward-a-colour), and a strip and a number field for [its brightness](#set-a-wheels-brightness). Every value starts at 0, which leaves the picture unchanged.
414	
415	The wheels apply after **Color** and **Light**, and before the [curves](/color/curves/) and the [look](/color/looks/). Their order is fixed.
416	
417	## What each wheel moves
418	
419	| Wheel | What it moves | Brightness at +1 | Brightness at −1 |
420	| --- | --- | --- | --- |
421	| **Lift** | Moves black and holds white, so it mostly affects the shadows. | Black rises to 25 %. | Everything below 20 % goes to black. |
422	| **Gamma** | Moves the middle tones and holds both ends. | A 50 % grey rises to about 71 %. | A 50 % grey falls to 25 %. |
423	| **Gain** | Moves white and holds black, so it mostly affects the highlights. | Every level is multiplied by 1.5. | Every level is halved, so white falls to 50 %. |
424	
425	A push follows the same rule. On **Lift** it tints the blacks and leaves white alone, and on **Gain** it tints the whites and leaves black alone.
426	
427	## Push a range toward a colour
428	
429	Press anywhere on a disc and drag. The direction you drag picks the hue, and the distance from the centre sets the strength. To warm the highlights, for example, drag **Gain**'s puck a little toward orange, between the red at the top of the disc and the yellow on its left.
430	
431	The square puck moves by however far the pointer moves. It doesn't jump to where you pressed, and a press with no drag changes nothing. Dragging one disc radius gives the full push, and past the rim the puck slides along the rim.
432	
433	A puck changes only that wheel's colour, never its brightness. One drag is one undo step, named after the wheel, such as **Undo Lift**.
434	
435	## Set a wheel's brightness
436	
437	The strip and the field under each disc set that wheel's master brightness, from −1 to +1. The default is 0.
438	
439	- **Click the strip** off the knob and the value jumps there.
440	- **Drag the knob** and it moves from where it stands, with no jump.
441	- **Type in the field** for an exact value. It shows two decimals and has no unit. Return, Tab or a click elsewhere saves it, and <kbd>Esc</kbd> keeps the old value. A number past either end is set to −1 or 1, and anything that isn't a number is ignored.
442	
443	A drag is one undo step and so is a typed value, each named after its wheel.
444	
445	## Make a fine adjustment
446	
447	Hold <kbd>⌥</kbd> while you drag a puck or a strip to move at a tenth of the speed. On a strip, a press with <kbd>⌥</kbd> held moves the value relative to where it stands, with no jump.
448	
449	On a disc you can press or let go of <kbd>⌥</kbd> at any point in a drag. On a strip, letting go of <kbd>⌥</kbd> before the mouse sends the knob back under the pointer.
450	
451	The same key slows a point on a [curve](/color/curves/) and a handle on a [qualifier](/color/qualifiers/).
452	
453	## Read the push
454	
455	Hover a disc to see its push as a hue angle and a strength, such as **Hue 34° · 0.25**. A centred puck reads **Neutral**.
456	
457	The angle counts from red at 0°, with green at 120° and blue at 240°. The strength runs from 0 at the centre to 1 at the rim. The push has no number field, so this is the only place in the inspector to read it as a number.
458	
459	## Wheels match the vectorscope
460	
461	Each disc is turned so that a hue sits where the [vectorscope](/color/vectorscope/) draws it. Dragging toward a colour moves the trace toward that colour.
462	
463	Red sits 103° counter-clockwise from 3 o'clock, just left of the top. Going counter-clockwise from there you'll find yellow on the left, green at the lower left, cyan near the bottom, blue on the right and magenta at the upper right. Every 75 % target on the vectorscope falls within about 12° of its place on the disc.
464	
465	## Reset the wheels
466	
467	| To reset | Do this |
468	| --- | --- |
469	| One wheel's push | Double-click its disc. The puck returns to the centre and the wheel's brightness stays. |
470	| One wheel's brightness | Double-click its strip. The value returns to 0 and the push stays. |
471	| All three wheels | Choose **Reset** in the section's header, or right-click the wheels and choose **Reset to default**. **Reset** appears once a wheel has moved, while no action is selected. |
472	
473	Each of these is one undo step, even when the first click of a double-click on the strip moved the knob. A double-click is named after its wheel, and resetting all three shows as **Undo Wheels**.
474	
475	## Grade several clips at once
476	
477	Select the clips and use the wheels as usual. Each control changes only its own values. A puck gives every selected clip that wheel's push and leaves each clip's brightness and other wheels alone. A strip or a field does the same for that wheel's brightness.
478	
479	The controls show the first clip's values. When the clips differ on any wheel, a **mixed** badge appears. One badge covers all three wheels.
480	
481	## Animate the wheels
482	
483	With an action selected, a puck, a strip or a field sets the action's end value, and the wheels ramp there from their values at the action's start. See [Animate a grade](/color/animate-a-grade/).
484	
485	While the action animates the wheels, a disc shows a hollow square at the start value and the puck in the action colour. A strip fills in the action colour from the start value. A coral mark shows the value under the playhead when it differs.
486	
487	The three wheels count as one row of the action. Moving any of them puts one [◆ in the gutter](/motion/edit-an-action/#read-the-row-marks) beside all three, and removing the row takes all three out of the action. Right-click them for **Remove from action N** or **Set end value to default**, or choose **Clear** in the section's header.
488	
489	## Good to know
490	
491	There's no Offset wheel. For an overall lift, use **Brightness** in the [Color section](/color/color-section/).
492	
493	## With an agent
494	
495	An agent can set the wheels with `set_video` as exact numbers, and an agent is the only way to enter a push by number. Each wheel takes a push as `x` and `y` and a brightness as `master`, all from −1 to 1. Its angles count the way the tooltip does, with red at 0° along positive `x`, and aren't turned to match the disc.
496	
497	Any wheel or value it leaves out stays as it is. Frame Job won't take a push past the rim from `set_video`, and says so rather than moving it to the rim. An action's end set with `set_action_end` is different: the value is kept, and the push stops at the rim while the action plays. See [Tools: picture and grade](/mcp/tools-set-video/#wheels).
498

514	Curves change the picture's tones with points on a line. Use **Master** for contrast and the black and white points, and **Red**, **Green** and **Blue** to work on one colour at a time. The picture goes through the curves after the [wheels](/color/wheels/) and before the [look](/color/looks/).

522	<Shot
523	  name="05g-clip-curves.inspector"
524	  alt="The Curves section open on the Color tab. Six cells read Master, Red, Green, Blue, Hue and Sat, with Master chosen and a dot under Master and Red. 527	## The Curves section
528	
529	Select a video, image or still clip, or an [adjustment clip](/color/adjustment-clips/), open the [Color tab](/color/color-tab/) and open **Curves**. The section starts closed, and its header reads "neutral" until a curve changes, then "adjusted".
530	
531	The section has three parts, from top to bottom:
532	
533	- The channel picker, which chooses the curve you're editing.
534	- The plot, a square with a 4 × 4 grid. It grows with the inspector up to 300 pt wide.
535	- The selected point's **In** and **Out** fields, and **Delete**.
536	
537	Across the plot is the level going in, from 0 at the left to 1 at the right. Up the plot is the level coming out. A thin diagonal marks a straight curve, which changes nothing.
538	
539	## The channel picker
540	
541	Six cells above the plot choose the channel you edit. Click a different cell, and any selected point is deselected.
542	
543	| Cell | What it changes |
544	| --- | --- |
545	| **Master** | All three colours together. Use it for contrast and for the black and white points. |
546	| **Red** | The red channel only. |
547	| **Green** | The green channel only. |
548	| **Blue** | The blue channel only. |
549	| **Hue** | Hue vs Hue, which turns a chosen hue toward another. See [Hue vs Hue and Hue vs Sat curves](/color/hue-curves/). |
550	| **Sat** | Hue vs Sat, which saturates or mutes a chosen hue. See [Hue vs Hue and Hue vs Sat curves](/color/hue-curves/). |
551	
552	**Master**, **Red**, **Green** and **Blue** are the tone curves, and **Hue** and **Sat** are the hue curves.
553	
554	There's no separate luma curve. **Master** runs first, then each colour goes through its own channel, so a **Red** curve works on what **Master** has already done.
555	
556	The chosen cell is framed and labelled in its channel's colour. A new window starts on **Master**, and the plot stays on your channel while the window is open. The choice isn't saved with the project.
557	
558	### See which channels are changed
559	
560	A dot under a cell means that channel has been changed.
561	
562	Changed channels also show as faint lines in their own colour behind the curve you're editing. **Master**, **Red**, **Green** and **Blue** show behind each other. **Hue** and **Sat** each have their own scale, so neither shows behind the other.
563	
564	## Shape the picture
565	
566	| To | Do this |
567	| --- | --- |
568	| Add contrast | On **Master**, make a gentle S: pull a point low on the curve down, and a point high on the curve up. |
569	| Set the black point | On **Master**, drag the first point right along the bottom. Everything darker than its **In** comes out black. |
570	| Set the white point | On **Master**, drag the last point left along the top. Everything brighter than its **In** comes out white. |
571	| Lift the blacks | On **Master**, drag the first point up the left edge. |
572	| Warm the shadows | On **Red**, drag the first point up the left edge. |
573	| Take out a colour cast | On the channel that's too strong, add a point in the middle of the curve and pull it down. |
574	
575	## Edit points
576	
577	A curve holds from 2 to 16 points. It runs smoothly through every point and never overshoots, so between two points it stays between their values. Past the first and last points, a tone curve stays flat.
578	
579	Each drag, nudge, deletion or typed value is one undo step, and **Edit ▸ Undo** reads **Undo Curves**.
580	
581	### Add a point
582	
583	Click the plot away from any point. Frame Job adds a point on the curve, directly above or below your click, and selects it. Keep the button down and the same press drags it.
584	
585	A double-click on the curve itself adds one point. A double-click away from the curve adds two, side by side, because the second click misses the first point.
586	
587	A 17th point beeps, and so does a click with no room left between two points.
588	
589	On a straight channel, the new point isn't saved until you move it, nudge it or type a value, so a stray click changes nothing. It stays on the plot while it's selected, and it goes when you deselect it or change channel. You can click several in a row to pin a straight curve before you bend it, and they're all saved with the first one you move.
590	
591	On a channel that already has a shape, the click saves the new point straight away. The point lies on the curve, so the picture changes very little, if at all.
592	
593	### Drag a point
594	
595	Press a point to grab it where it stands, with no jump, and drag. It stays inside the plot and can't pass its neighbours. The closest it gets to a neighbour across the plot is 0.001 on a tone curve and 0.1° on a hue curve.
596	
597	You can drag the end points too.
598	
599	### Fine drag and axis lock
600	
601	Hold <kbd>⌥</kbd> while you drag to move the point at a tenth of the speed.
602	
603	Hold <kbd>⇧</kbd> while you drag to lock the point to one axis. It stays put until the pointer has travelled 4 pt from the press, and then whichever direction you moved further wins for the rest of the drag. Let go of <kbd>⇧</kbd> and the point follows the pointer again.
604	
605	<kbd>⌥</kbd> and <kbd>⇧</kbd> combine.
606	
607	### Nudge a point
608	
609	With a point selected, the arrow keys nudge it. Hold <kbd>⇧</kbd> to go ten times as far. Each press is one undo step.
610	
611	| Channel | Arrow key | With <kbd>⇧</kbd> |
612	| --- | --- | --- |
613	| **Master**, **Red**, **Green**, **Blue** | 0.01 | 0.1 |
614	| **Hue** | 1° | 10° |
615	| **Sat** | 1° across, 0.01 up and down | 10° across, 0.1 up and down |
616	
617	### In and Out fields
618	
619	The **In** and **Out** fields below the plot let you type the selected point's position. With no point selected, they're blank and disabled.
620	
621	| Channel | **In** | **Out** |
622	| --- | --- | --- |
623	| **Master**, **Red**, **Green**, **Blue** | 0 to 1, three decimals | 0 to 1, three decimals |
624	| **Hue** | 0° to 359.9°, one decimal | −180° to +180°, one decimal |
625	| **Sat** | 0° to 359.9°, one decimal | 0× to 2×, two decimals |
626	
627	A number outside the range goes to the nearest end of it, and an **In** past a neighbouring point stops short of that point.
628	
629	### Delete a point
630	
631	Select the point and press <kbd>⌫</kbd> or <kbd>⌦</kbd>, choose **Delete** below the plot, or double-click the point.
632	
633	A curve can't go below two points. The keys and the double-click beep, and **Delete** is greyed out.
634	
635	### Deselect a point
636	
637	Press <kbd>Esc</kbd>, or click another channel. This also hands the keyboard back to the editor.
638	
639	### The plot and the keyboard
640	
641	While a point is selected the plot has the keyboard, so:
642	
643	- The arrow keys nudge the point rather than move the playhead.
644	- <kbd>⌫</kbd> deletes the point, not the selected clip.
645	
646	Keys the plot doesn't use still reach the editor, so <kbd>Space</kbd> still plays.
647	
648	## Hover readout
649	
650	While the pointer is over the plot, and during a drag, a small label shows the pointer's position and the curve's value there.
651	
652	| Channel | The label reads |
653	| --- | --- |
654	| **Master**, **Red**, **Green**, **Blue** | `In 0.42 → Out 0.47` |
655	| **Hue** | `Hue 34° → +12°` |
656	| **Sat** | `Hue 120° → ×0.80` |
657	
658	There's no label outside the plot, and that includes the spectrum strip under a hue channel.
659	
660	## Reset curves
661	
662	To straighten one channel, right-click its cell in the picker and choose **Reset Master**, **Reset Red**, **Reset Green**, **Reset Blue**, **Reset Hue** or **Reset Sat**. The item is greyed out while that channel is already straight.
663	
664	To straighten all six channels, choose **Reset** in the section's header. It shows while a curve is changed, and it's one undo step. You can also right-click the plot and choose **Reset to default**.
665	
666	## Curves inside an action
667	
668	With an [action](/motion/actions/) selected, a curve edit goes to the action's end, so the curve animates. Any two curves animate into each other, whatever their number of points, and so does a curve and a straight line.
669	
670	The plot shows it in its own way: the action's start curve is dashed, and the edited curve and its points are in the action colour.
671	
672	To animate a curve back to neutral, right-click a cell and choose its **Reset** item, or right-click the plot and choose **Set end value to default**. Each writes a straight curve to the action's end, for the channels that aren't already straight. The section's **Reset** isn't there while the action is selected. **Clear** takes its place once the action animates curves, and removes them from the action.
673	
674	See [Animate a grade](/color/animate-a-grade/).
675	
676	## Good to know
677	
678	With several clips selected, the plot shows the first clip's curves, and the section shows **mixed** when they differ. An edit gives every selected clip the curve you're editing, for that channel, and leaves their other channels alone.
679	
680	Selecting another clip deselects the point.
681	
682	## With an agent
683	
684	An agent writes a whole channel at once as a list of 2 to 16 points, and that list replaces the channel. Sending `null` for a channel removes its curve, and a list that changes nothing is stored as no curve.
685	
686	A drag stops at a limit, but an agent's value outside the limits gets an error and the curve stays as it was. An action's end is the exception: the value is kept, and it's moved to the nearest limit as the action plays. See [Tools: picture and grade](/mcp/tools-set-video/#curves).
687	
688	## Related
689

691	- [Wheels](/color/wheels/)
692	- [Looks](/color/looks/)

697	title: Hue vs Hue and Hue vs Sat curves
698	description: Turn one colour toward another, or saturate or mute it, without touching the rest of the picture.
699	---
700	
701	import { Steps } from '@astrojs/starlight/components';
702	import AtAGlance from '@components/AtAGlance.astro';
703	
704	The hue curves work on one colour at a time. **Hue** turns a chosen hue toward another, such as making the greens more teal. **Sat** saturates or mutes a chosen hue, such as calming a loud red. Both leave the other colours alone.
705	
706	<AtAGlance
707	  where="Clip tab ▸ Color ▸ Curves ▸ the Hue and Sat cells"
708	  tools={['set_video', 'set_action_end']}
709	/>
710	
711	## The two hue channels
712	
713	The **Hue** and **Sat** cells in the channel picker put the plot into degrees. Each channel lays the colours out across the plot, and its height says what happens to the colour at that position.
714	
715	| Cell | Curve | Across | Up | The centre line |
716	| --- | --- | --- | --- | --- |
717	| **Hue** | Hue vs Hue | Hue, 0° to 360° | A shift, −180° to +180° | 0°, no shift |
718	| **Sat** | Hue vs Sat | Hue, 0° to 360° | A gain, 0× to 2× | 1×, unchanged |
719	
720	So a straight hue channel is a flat line across the middle, not a diagonal. It starts with two points on that line, at 0° and 180°.
721	
722	Points work as they do on any curve: click to add one, drag, nudge, type, delete and reset. See [Master and RGB curves](/color/curves/#edit-points). A channel holds 2 to 16 points.
723	
724	The hue curves run after **Master**, **Red**, **Green** and **Blue** and before the [look](/color/looks/), so they read each colour as those curves left it. Both hue curves read that colour once, before either changes it. A **Sat** point on the greens still acts on greens you've turned teal with **Hue**.
725	
726	## The spectrum strip
727	
728	A strip under the plot shows which colour each position stands for, from 0° at the left to 360° at the right. Thin lines mark every 60°, with lines across at the quarters and a stronger line at the centre.
729	
730	| Hue | Colour |
731	| --- | --- |
732	| 0° | Red |
733	| 60° | Yellow |
734	| 120° | Green |
735	| 180° | Cyan |
736	| 240° | Blue |
737	| 300° | Magenta |
738	
739	## Hue vs Hue
740	
741	A positive shift moves a colour to the right along the strip, from red toward yellow and green. A negative shift moves it to the left. Brightness stays as it was.
742	
743	To make the greens more teal:
744	
745	<Steps>
746	
747	1. Select the clip, open the [Color tab](/color/color-tab/), open **Curves** and click the **Hue** cell.
748	
749	2. Click the plot at about 90° and again at about 150°, without dragging. These two points hold the colours either side still.
750	
751	3. Press the centre line at about 120° and drag up. The label beside the pointer shows the shift, such as `Hue 120° → +30°`.
752	
753	</Steps>
754	
755	The outer points are saved with the first point you move. Without them, the shift spreads as far as the points at 0° and 180°.
756	
757	## Hue vs Sat
758	
759	Above the centre line a hue gets more saturated, and below it less. At the bottom of the plot, 0×, that hue goes grey. At the top, 2×, its saturation doubles. Saturation scales around the colour's own brightness.
760	
761	To mute the reds:
762	
763	<Steps>
764	
765	1. With **Curves** open on the clip, click the **Sat** cell.
766	
767	2. Click the plot at about 330° and again at about 30°, without dragging. These two points hold the colours either side still.
768	
769	3. Drag the point at 0°, at the left end of the centre line, down. The label beside the pointer shows the gain, such as `Hue 0° → ×0.60`.
770	
771	</Steps>
772	
773	## Hue curve safeguards
774	
775	- **A grey stays grey.** A grey has no real hue to read, so a hue curve never tints it. When a colour's strongest and weakest channels are within 2% of each other it's left alone, and the effect fades in to full strength at 6%.
776	- **Points never cross the wrap.** A point stops at 0° and 359.9°, so it can't slide round to the other end. The curve itself does wrap: its right end runs on smoothly into its left end, so a shift around red covers both ends of the plot.
777	- **Colours stay in range.** When a turned colour can't keep its brightness, it gives up some saturation rather than clip.
778	
779	## Good to know
780	
781	- The closest a point gets to a neighbour across the plot is 0.1°.
782	- **Reset Hue** and **Reset Sat** straighten one channel from the cell's right-click menu. The section's **Reset** straightens all six, the tone curves included. See [Reset curves](/color/curves/#reset-curves).
783	- The **Hue** slider in the [Color section](/color/color-section/) turns every colour at once. Hue vs Hue turns only the colours you choose.
784	- Hue curves animate inside an action as tone curves do. See [Animate a grade](/color/animate-a-grade/).
785	
786	## With an agent
787	
788	An agent writes `hue_hue` and `hue_sat` whole, each as a list of 2 to 16 hue and value pairs, and that list replaces the channel. It can place a point anywhere from 0 up to, but not including, 360. A value outside the limits gets an error and the curve stays as it was. An action's end is the exception: the value is kept, and it's moved to the nearest limit as the action plays. See [Tools: picture and grade](/mcp/tools-set-video/#curves).
789

18	## Apply a look
19	
20	<Steps>
21	
22	1. Select one or more clips.
23	
24	2. Open the **Color** sub-tab of the [Clip tab](/color/color-tab/), and open **Look**, its last section. It starts closed.
25	
26	3. Click a tile.
27	
28	4. Drag [**Amount**](#amount) until the look sits right.
29	
30	</Steps>
31	
32	<Shot
33	  name="05d-clip-look.inspector"
34	  alt="The Look section of the Color sub-tab. A 3 by 3 grid of thumbnail tiles reads None, Warm, Cool, Teal & Orange, Vivid, Faded, Vintage, Dramatic and Black & White, with Teal & Orange outlined in blue. Below the grid are the Import LUT… button and an Amount slider at 80%. The section header reads Teal & Orange 80%, beside a Reset button."
35	/>
36	
37	The look goes on every selected clip as one undo step, **Look**. A clip that already had a look keeps its amount, and a clip with no look gets 100%.
38	
39	## The Look gallery
40	
41	The gallery is a 3 × 3 grid: **None** first, then the eight looks. Each tile is a [thumbnail](#live-thumbnails) of the first selected clip with that look on it, so you choose by eye. The tile of the look every selected clip shares is outlined in the accent colour, and **None** is outlined when no selected clip has a look. When the clips disagree, no tile is outlined.
42	
43	Under the grid comes an **Imported** group, if the project holds any LUTs, and then **Import LUT…**. See [.cube LUTs](/color/luts/).
44	
45	## The eight looks
46	
47	Each look is Frame Job's own, built from the same kinds of adjustment as its tone controls. Most also push a tint into the shadows, the highlights or both.
48	
49	| Look | What it does |
50	| --- | --- |
51	| **Warm** | A warmer white balance, a little more vibrance and golden highlights. |
52	| **Cool** | A cooler white balance, a touch more contrast and blue shadows. |
53	| **Teal & Orange** | Teal shadows and orange highlights, with more contrast and vibrance. |
54	| **Vivid** | More contrast and strong vibrance, with deeper blacks and brighter whites. |
55	| **Faded** | Low contrast, muted colour, softer highlights and lifted blacks, for a washed-out picture. |
56	| **Vintage** | Muted and warm, with a fade, green-tinted shadows and yellow-tinted highlights. |
57	| **Dramatic** | Darker, contrasty and desaturated, with cool shadows. |
58	| **Black & White** | All colour removed, with more contrast, brighter whites and deeper blacks. |
59	
60	## Live thumbnails
61	
62	Each tile shows what clicking it would give you. It's the real frame as an export would draw it, with that tile applied to the selected clips, at the amount they'd keep. A clip at 40% shows you every tile at 40%.
63	
64	The frame is the one at the playhead when the playhead is inside the first selected clip. Otherwise it's that clip's first frame.
65	
66	A refresh starts about 0.3 seconds after the playhead stops or an edit lands. That wait begins again each time the frame changes, so the tiles don't refresh while playback or a scrub moves through the clip. They only render while the Look section is open, so closing the section cancels any render in progress.
67	
68	The thumbnails always show the graded picture, even with [Show Ungraded](/color/show-ungraded/) on.
69	
70	## Amount
71	
72	**Amount** sets how much of the look applies, from 0 to 100%. Use the slider, type in the field, or choose 0, 25, 50, 75 or 100% behind the field's chevron.
73	
74	The row only appears when every selected clip has a look. At 0% the look stays on the clip and draws nothing, so you can bring it back later at any amount.
75	
76	Amount is the one Look control that animates. Select an action and the value you set goes to the action's end, so the look fades in or out. See [Animate a grade](/color/animate-a-grade/).
77	
78	## Remove a look
79	
80	Do any one of these:
81	
82	- Click the **None** tile.
83	- Click **Reset** in the section's header. It's there when a selected clip has a look and no action is selected.
84	- Choose **Clip ▸ Look ▸ None**.
85	
86	The look comes off every selected clip as one undo step, **Look**. The rest of the grade stays.
87	
88	## Apply a look from the menu
89	
90	**Clip ▸ Look** does what the gallery does: the eight looks, then any imported LUTs, then **None**.
91	
92	A checkmark marks the look every selected clip carries, and a dash marks one that only some of them carry. **None** is checked when no selected clip has a look. No item has a keyboard shortcut.
93	
94	The menu is available when a selected clip can take a grade. If the selection also holds clips that can't, such as a title, those clips are left alone. The **Color** sub-tab doesn't show for a selection like that, so the menu is the way to reach the gallery's looks.
95	
96	## The Look summary
97	
98	The section's header tells you what's on the selection, even with the section closed.
99	
100	| The header reads | What it means |
101	| --- | --- |
102	| **Warm 80%** | Every selected clip has that look at that amount. A LUT shows its name, such as **Warm Print 80%**. |
103	| **none** | No selected clip has a look. |
104	| **mixed** | The selected clips differ, in their look or in its amount. |
105	
106	## Looks on stills and adjustment clips
107	
108	A look works on video, image and still clips, and on adjustment clips. The gallery and the menu don't offer one for text, shapes, graphics or nests.
109	
110	On an [adjustment clip](/color/adjustment-clips/), the look grades everything behind the clip, for as long as the clip lasts. The clip's **Strength** scales it along with the rest of its grade, and a [qualifier](/color/qualifiers/) narrows it to the colours the qualifier selects. That's also the way to put a look over a title, or over several clips at once.
111	
112	## Good to know
113	
114	- A clip has one look at a time. Picking another replaces it, whether it's a built-in look or a LUT.
115	- A look comes after Light, Color, the wheels and the curves, so it grades your corrected picture. It comes before the Sepia, Noir, Vignette and Invert [filters](/effects/filters/).
116	- With an action selected, a tile and **None** still change the clip's own look, not the action. **Reset** is hidden then, and the header shows **Clear** instead when the action animates **Amount**.
117	- [Show Ungraded](/color/show-ungraded/) takes the look out of the preview only. Nothing about the clip changes, and an export still has the look.
118	- [Paste Attributes](/editing/paste-attributes/) copies a clip's look and its amount along with the rest of its picture settings. See [Copy a grade](/color/copy-a-grade/).
119	
120	## With an agent
121	
122	An agent sets a look by its kind with `set_video`, for example `{look: {kind: "teal_orange", amount: 0.6}}`, and removes it with `{look: null}`. The kinds are `warm`, `cool`, `teal_orange`, `vivid`, `faded`, `vintage`, `dramatic` and `black_white`, and `lut` for an [imported LUT](/color/luts/#with-an-agent).
123	
124	`amount` runs from 0 to 1. Left out, a clip keeps the amount it had, or takes 1 if it had no look. An amount on its own needs a clip that already has a look. A misspelt kind or an amount outside 0 to 1 gives an error and changes nothing.
125	
126	An agent can also do something the gallery can't: put a different look at an action's end with `set_action_end`. A change to another look switches at the end of the action instead of blending, its amount included. See [Tools: picture and grade](/mcp/tools-set-video/#look).
127

138	title: ".cube LUTs"
139	description: "Bring a .cube colour table into a project, use it as a clip's look, and know what happens when the file changes, goes missing or is removed."
140	---
141	
142	import { Steps } from '@astrojs/starlight/components';
143	import AtAGlance from '@components/AtAGlance.astro';
144	import Shot from '@components/Shot.astro';
145	
146	A LUT (look-up table) is a table that turns each colour in the picture into another. Use a `.cube` LUT to bring in a grade from another grading tool, a camera maker or a LUT pack. In Frame Job it's a file in your project, like footage. You add it once, then use it as a clip's [look](/color/looks/), or as the conversion for a [log file](/hdr/log-luts/).
147	
148	<AtAGlance
149	  menu={['Clip ▸ Look', 'File ▸ Add Media…']}
150	  keys="⇧⌘I"
151	  where={['Clip tab ▸ Color ▸ Look ▸ Import LUT…', 'Media tab']}
152	  tools={['import_media', 'set_video', 'remove_media']}
153	/>
154	
155	## Import and apply a LUT
156	
157	<Steps>
158	
159	1. Select the clips you want to grade.
160	
161	2. Open the **Look** section of the **Color** sub-tab, and click **Import LUT…** under the gallery. The sub-tab doesn't show if the selection holds a text, shape, graphic or nest clip.
162	
163	3. Choose a `.cube` file.
164	
165	</Steps>
166	
167	<Shot
168	  name="05e-clip-look-lut.inspector"
169	  alt="The Look section with the eight built-in look tiles and None, then an Imported group holding two tiles, Warm Print and Bleach, with Warm Print outlined in blue. The Import LUT… button sits underneath, and the section header reads Warm Print 80%."
170	/>
171	
172	The file joins the project and goes on the selected clips as one undo step, **Import LUT**. If the file is already in the project, Frame Job reuses its entry rather than adding it twice. If Frame Job can't read the file, an error appears and nothing changes.
173	
174	## Add a LUT without applying it
175	
176	Add the file to the project and apply it later:
177	
178	- Choose **File ▸ Add Media…** (<kbd>⇧⌘I</kbd>). A file with the `.cube` extension, in any case, counts as a LUT.
179	- Or drop the file on the **Media** tab. It's the only place in the window that takes a dropped `.cube`.
180	
181	## Apply a LUT already in the project
182	
183	Every LUT in the project is offered in two places, in the order it was added, however the Media tab is sorted:
184	
185	- **The gallery.** Its tile sits in the **Imported** group, in rows of three, and previews the LUT on your frame like any [live thumbnail](/color/looks/#live-thumbnails). The tile's name is the file's name without `.cube`. With no LUTs in the project, the group isn't there.
186	- **The menu.** It's an item in **Clip ▸ Look**, between the eight looks and **None**.
187	
188	Both work as they do for a built-in look, on every selected clip, as one undo step, **Look**.
189	
190	## A LUT is a look
191	
192	A LUT applied to a clip behaves like a built-in look. It comes at the same point in the grade, uses the same [**Amount**](/color/looks/#amount) row, and is removed the same way. A clip that had a look keeps its amount, and a clip with none gets 100%. A clip holds one look, so a LUT replaces a built-in look, and a built-in look replaces a LUT. A LUT also [travels with a paste](/color/copy-a-grade/#luts-travel-with-a-paste) into another project.
193	
194	## LUT rows on the Media tab
195	
196	A LUT appears in the [Media tab](/projects/media-tab/) with a cube icon, and its tooltip reads "A LUT: apply it to clips as a look."
197	
198	A LUT never goes on the timeline. You can't drag its row, **Insert at Playhead** and **Overwrite at Playhead** are off in its right-click menu, and the same commands in the menu bar stay dimmed while its row is selected.
199	
200	The rest of the row works as it does for footage:
201	
202	- **Reveal in Timeline** selects the timeline clips whose look it is.
203	- **Reveal in Finder** shows the file, and **Relink…** points the entry at a new one. A LUT relinks only to another `.cube` file.
204	- **Unused only** leaves out a LUT that a clip's look or a file's Camera Log uses.
205	- [Consolidate Media](/projects/consolidate-media/) copies the file into the project with everything else.
206	
207	## Supported .cube files
208	
209	Frame Job reads 3D LUTs in a text `.cube` file of up to 32 MiB.
210	
211	| In the file | What Frame Job does |
212	| --- | --- |
213	| `LUT_3D_SIZE` from 2 to 65 | Reads it. The line is required, and it comes before the table. |
214	| `TITLE`, `#` comments, blank lines | Reads past them. |
215	| Windows line endings or a UTF-8 byte order mark | Reads them. |
216	| `DOMAIN_MIN 0 0 0`, `DOMAIN_MAX 1 1 1`, `LUT_3D_INPUT_RANGE 0 1` | Accepts them, because they're the defaults. |
217	| Table values outside 0 to 1 | Accepts them, and clamps them to 0 to 1 when drawing. |
218	
219	Frame Job won't take anything else. It shows an error, usually naming the line it stopped at, and the file stays out of the project. That covers:
220	
221	- A file that isn't text, or is over 32 MiB.
222	- A 1D LUT.
223	- A `LUT_3D_SIZE` outside 2 to 65, or a second `LUT_3D_SIZE` line.
224	- A domain or input range that isn't the default.
225	- A keyword Frame Job doesn't know, or any keyword after the table.
226	- A table with too few or too many rows, or a row without three numbers.
227	- A value that isn't a finite number.
228	
229	The message reads, for example, "“Film.cube” is not a LUT Frame Job reads: line 2: LUT_3D_SIZE 200 is outside 2–65."
230	
231	## Warnings in the Look section
232	
233	The section warns you in two cases. Neither stops you, and the LUT still applies.
234	
235	| The warning | When it shows | What it means |
236	| --- | --- | --- |
237	| "This clip's file is converted by Camera Log; a camera LUT here converts it twice." | A selected clip's look is a LUT and its file has a [Camera Log](/hdr/camera-log/) setting, or is a PQ file. | A creative LUT is fine there. A camera LUT would convert the footage a second time. |
238	| "This project is HDR (HLG): a .cube LUT reads its values as Rec. 709." | A selected clip's look is a LUT and the [project is HDR](/hdr/dynamic-range/). | The LUT's values keep their 0-to-1 meaning. Frame Job doesn't adapt them for HDR. |
239	
240	## A changed file
241	
242	Frame Job reads the `.cube` file where it is. If you change the file on disk, the new table is read the next time a frame is drawn. There's nothing to import again.
243	
244	## A missing or broken file
245	
246	If the file goes missing, or can't be read any more, the clip draws without its look. The rest of its grade still applies, and the look stays on the clip. A clip's look comes back once the file is back.
247	
248	A missing LUT shows the **missing** badge in the Media tab, and it's in the list Frame Job offers to [relink](/projects/relink-media/) when the project opens. A file that's there but broken has no badge, and the look doesn't draw until you fix the file or relink it.
249	
250	## Remove a LUT in use
251	
252	A LUT counts as used by every clip whose look it is, on the timeline or in a nest, and by every file whose Camera Log it is.
253	
254	<Steps>
255	
256	1. In the Media tab, right-click the LUT's row and choose **Remove**.
257	
258	2. Read the alert, which counts the clips that would lose the look and the files that would lose their Camera Log. For example, "It is the look of 3 clips, which keep their place and lose the look."
259	
260	3. Choose **Remove and Clear Looks**, or **Cancel**.
261	
262	</Steps>
263	
264	**Remove and Clear Looks** removes the LUT, clears the look from those clips and clears the Camera Log from those files, as one undo step, **Remove Media**. The clips stay where they are. An unused LUT is removed straight away, with no alert.
265	
266	## With an agent
267	
268	An agent adds the file with `import_media`, then applies it with `set_video`, naming the media id `import_media` gave it: `{look: {kind: "lut", media: 9}}`. `media` is required with `lut`, and it's an error with any other kind.
269	
270	An agent can't place a LUT as a clip. `add_clip`, `insert_clip`, `overwrite_clip` and `add_background` give an error that says how to apply it instead. `remove_media` won't remove a LUT in use unless the call sets `with_clips`, which clears those uses as **Remove and Clear Looks** does.
271	
272	An agent can also name a LUT at an action's end. That action stays if the LUT is removed, and draws no look at its end. See [Tools: picture and grade](/mcp/tools-set-video/#look) and [Tools: media](/mcp/tools-media/#remove_media).
273
