283	title: Qualifiers
284	description: Limit an adjustment clip's grade to the pixels of one colour or brightness, using hue, saturation and luma ranges.
285	---
286	
287	import { Steps } from '@astrojs/starlight/components';
288	import AtAGlance from '@components/AtAGlance.astro';
289	import Shot from '@components/Shot.astro';
290	
291	A qualifier limits an [adjustment clip](/color/adjustment-clips/)'s grade to the pixels behind it that match up to three ranges of hue, saturation and luma. Use it to change one colour and leave the rest of the picture alone.
292	
293	<AtAGlance
294	  where="Clip tab ▸ Color ▸ Qualifier"
295	  tools={['set_video', 'set_action_end', 'render_frame']}
296	  needs="Every selected clip must be an adjustment clip."
297	/>
298	
299	<Shot
300	  name="05h-clip-qualifier.inspector"
301	  alt="The Qualifier section of an adjustment clip, its header reading hue · sat. Hue is ticked at Centre 25°, Width 30°, Soft 15°, and Saturation at Low 0.15, High 1.00, Soft 0.05. Each strip is dimmed outside its range. Luma is unticked, with a dimmed strip and greyed-out fields. Below are Invert, Blur at 0%, the Pick from Canvas button and a ticked Show Selection."
302	/>
303	
304	## Grade one colour
305	
306	<Steps>
307	
308	1. Put an [adjustment clip](/color/adjustment-clips/#insert-an-adjustment-clip) above the picture, for the span you want.
309	
310	2. With the clip selected, give it a grade in the **Color** sub-tab. A qualifier on its own changes nothing, because it only narrows a grade.
311	
312	3. Open the **Qualifier** section by clicking its header if it's [closed](/getting-started/inspector/#fold-a-section). Press **Pick from Canvas** and click the colour in the preview, or tick a range and set it by hand.
313	
314	4. Tick **Show Selection** to see what's picked. See [Show Selection](/color/show-selection/).
315	
316	5. Adjust the ranges until the selection is clean, then untick **Show Selection**.
317	
318	</Steps>
319	
320	A qualifier reaches every track behind the clip. To keep it to one area as well, [add a matte](/color/adjustment-clips/#confine-it-to-part-of-the-picture).
321	
322	## The Qualifier section
323	
324	The **Qualifier** section appears only when every selected clip is an adjustment clip, right after **Adjustment**. A picture clip can't have a qualifier.
325	
326	It holds the three ranges, then **Invert**, **Blur**, [Pick from Canvas](/color/pick-from-canvas/) and [Show Selection](/color/show-selection/).
327	
328	Matching reads the picture behind the clip as it was before the grade, so the grade never changes what it selects.
329	
330	### The Qualifier summary
331	
332	The section's header says what's set: the ranges that are on, then `inverted`, then the blur. For example, `hue · sat · inverted · blur 20%`. It reads `off` when nothing is set.
333	
334	**Reset** appears once anything is set, as long as no action is selected. It turns all three ranges off, clears **Invert** and sets **Blur** to 0 %, as one undo step named **Qualifier**.
335	
336	## Turn a range on
337	
338	Each range has a checkbox, a strip and three fields. Tick the checkbox and the range starts at its default. Ticking or unticking is one undo step named after the range.
339	
340	A range that's off has a dimmed strip that ignores presses, and greyed-out fields, so tick it first. Unticking forgets the range's values: tick it again and it's back at its default.
341	
342	## The three ranges
343	
344	| Range | Picks pixels by | Strip | Fields | Default when ticked |
345	| --- | --- | --- | --- | --- |
346	| **Hue** | Their colour | The colour spectrum, 0 to 360° | **Centre** 0 to 360°, **Width** 0 to 360°, **Soft** 0 to 180°, in whole degrees | Centre 30°, Width 50°, Soft 25° |
347	| **Saturation** | How colourful they are | Neutral to fully saturated | **Low**, **High** and **Soft**, 0 to 1, two decimals | Low 0, High 1, Soft 0.1 |
348	| **Luma** | How bright they are | Black to white | **Low**, **High** and **Soft**, 0 to 1, two decimals | Low 0, High 1, Soft 0.1 |
349	
350	A number typed outside a field's range is held at the nearest end of it.
351	
352	### Hue range
353	
354	**Centre** is the colour, and **Width** is how much of the spectrum around it is fully picked. **Soft** is the fall-off outside each edge. The default sits on skin tones: 5° to 55° is fully picked, fading to nothing at 340° and 80°.
355	
356	The band wraps round the spectrum, so a range centred on red picks from both ends of the strip.
357	
358	Greys are never picked by hue, because a grey has no colour to match. A colour fades out of a hue range as it nears grey, from a chroma of 0.06 down to 0.02 on a scale of 0 to 1.
359	
360	### Saturation range
361	
362	This is HSV saturation: 0 is neutral and 1 is fully saturated. **Low** and **High** are the edges of what's fully picked, and **Soft** is the fall-off outside each edge. At its default the range passes everything, so it does nothing until you narrow it.
363	
364	Near-black reads as 0, so dark noise doesn't count as colour. A range that starts above 0 leaves near-black pixels out.
365	
366	### Luma range
367	
368	This is brightness, from 0 for black to 1 for white, measured as Rec. 709 Y′. Its fields work as Saturation's do, and at its default it passes everything too.
369	
370	### Low and High never cross
371	
372	On **Saturation** and **Luma**, a typed **Low** is held at or below **High**, and a typed **High** at or above **Low**. Dragging stops at the same point.
373	
374	## How ranges combine
375	
376	A pixel has to fall inside every range that's on. Tick **Hue** and **Luma** and you get that colour at that brightness, not either one.
377	
378	Each range falls off smoothly across its **Soft** value outside each edge. The partial amounts multiply, so a pixel in the soft edge of two ranges is graded less than one in the soft edge of either. **Soft** at 0 gives a hard edge.
379	
380	## Use a strip
381	
382	Each strip is a live picture of its range, and the quickest way to set it.
383	
384	### Read a strip
385	
386	A strip shows its own scale: the spectrum for Hue, a neutral to red ramp for Saturation, black to white for Luma. It's dimmed 60 % outside the range and 30 % across the soft bands, so what stays bright is what's fully picked.
387	
388	The two block knobs mark the range's edges, and the two small squares mark where the softness runs out.
389	
390	### Drag a strip
391	
392	| Drag | What it changes |
393	| --- | --- |
394	| A block knob | On Hue, the **Width**, evenly about the centre. On Saturation and Luma, the **Low** or **High** edge. |
395	| A small square | **Soft** |
396	| The band between the knobs | Moves the whole range. Hue wraps round. Saturation and Luma stop at the ends of the scale, keeping their width. |
397	
398	A press within 5 pt of a handle grabs it, and if a knob and a square are both that close you get the knob. A press outside the band and away from every handle does nothing. When a range runs to the end of its scale, as Saturation and Luma do at their defaults, the square sits on the knob, so use the **Soft** field or narrow the range first.
399	
400	A drag is one undo step named after the range, and so is a number typed into a field.
401	
402	### Drag at a tenth of the speed
403	
404	Hold <kbd>⌥</kbd> while you drag to move a handle at a tenth of the speed.
405	
406	### Reset a range
407	
408	Double-click a strip to put the range back to its default. It stays on. To turn it off, untick it, or right-click the row and choose **Reset to default**.
409	
410	## Invert
411	
412	Tick **Invert** to grade everything except what the ranges pick. It's off by default. Use it to desaturate everything but one colour, for example.
413	
414	## Blur
415	
416	**Blur** softens the selection, not the picture. On noisy footage a speckled selection turns clean, and the grade blends into its surroundings.
417	
418	| Control | Range | Default |
419	| --- | --- | --- |
420	| **Blur** | 0 to 100 %, a slider and a field with presets at 0, 25, 50, 75 and 100 behind its chevron | 0 % |
421	
422	At 100 % the blur is a Gaussian of 24 pixels, measured on the canvas, so a Half or Quarter preview blurs the same share of the picture as an export. It's one undo step named **Qualifier Blur**.
423	
424	Blur never softens a [matte](/canvas/matte-tracks/) cutting the clip, and it does nothing while no range is on.
425	
426	## Animate a qualifier
427	
428	An [action](/motion/actions/) can animate a qualifier. Select an action on the clip's action lane, then change a control: the change goes to the action's end, and the numbers ramp there from the values the clip has when the action starts.
429	
430	- **Centre**, **Width**, **Soft**, **Low**, **High** and **Blur** ramp smoothly.
431	- The hue centre takes the short way round the spectrum, so 350° to 10° passes through 0°.
432	- A range turned on, and **Invert**, switch at the action's end. An action can't turn off a range the clip already has on.
433	
434	While an action animates the qualifier, a strip's band is outlined and its knobs are drawn in the action colour. The action holds the qualifier as one setting, so changing any row marks them all. See [Animate a grade](/color/animate-a-grade/).
435	
436	## Good to know
437	
438	- With several adjustment clips selected, the section shows the first clip's values and a badge marks the rows that differ. A change sends the whole range to every selected clip.
439	- **Invert** with no range on grades nothing, because every pixel counts as picked and Invert takes them all away.
440	- [Paste Attributes](/editing/paste-attributes/) copies a qualifier only from one adjustment clip to another. A picture clip gets none, and an adjustment clip keeps its own when the attributes come from a picture clip.
441	- In an [HDR project](/hdr/dynamic-range/), the ranges are measured on the HLG signal and Luma uses BT.2020's weights, so pick them again after switching a project's dynamic range.
442	
443	## With an agent
444	
445	`set_video` sets a qualifier through its `qualifier` key, on adjustment clips only. On any other clip it's an error naming the clip.
446	
447	| To | Send as `qualifier` |
448	| --- | --- |
449	| Turn a range on at its default | `{"hue": {}}` |
450	| Change part of a range and keep the rest | `{"hue": {"width": 30}}` |
451	| Turn a range off | `{"hue": null}` |
452	
453	`blur` runs from 0 to 1, where the inspector shows a percentage. A number outside its bounds is an error. It isn't held at the nearest end, as a typed number is.
454	
455	`render_frame` can draw the picture [Show Selection](/color/show-selection/) shows, for one adjustment clip, and `set_action_end` animates a qualifier. [Tools: picture and grade](/mcp/tools-set-video/#qualifier) lists every key.

465	title: "Show Selection"
466	description: "See in grey exactly which pixels an adjustment clip's qualifier picks, so you can tune its ranges before you judge the grade."
467	---
468	
469	import AtAGlance from '@components/AtAGlance.astro';
470	
471	Show Selection replaces the preview with a grey picture of what a [qualifier](/color/qualifiers/) picks. It shows you which pixels an adjustment clip's grade reaches, so you can tune the ranges without guessing from the graded picture.
472	
473	<AtAGlance
474	  menu="View ▸ Show Selection"
475	  where="Clip tab ▸ Color ▸ Qualifier ▸ Show Selection"
476	  tools="render_frame"
477	  needs="An adjustment clip selected."
478	/>
479	
480	## Turn it on
481	
482	Select an [adjustment clip](/color/adjustment-clips/), then tick **Show Selection** in the **Qualifier** section of the [Color tab](/color/color-tab/), or choose **View ▸ Show Selection**. Do the same again to turn it off. It's off to begin with and has no keyboard shortcut. The **Qualifier** section only appears while every selected clip is an adjustment clip.
483	
484	The checkbox and the menu item are the same switch, and the menu item has a checkmark while it's on. The menu item is dimmed while Show Selection is off and no adjustment clip is selected.
485	
486	## Read the picture
487	
488	| The preview shows | What it means |
489	| --- | --- |
490	| White | The clip's grade applies in full here. |
491	| Black | The grade doesn't touch this pixel. |
492	| Grey | The grade applies in part, as it does across a range's soft edge. |
493	
494	The picture is the selection as the clip really uses it, with a few things to keep in mind:
495	
496	- **Blur** and **Invert** are included, and so is any [matte](/canvas/matte-tracks/) cutting the clip.
497	- The clip's **Strength** isn't applied. A clip at 50 % still draws white where it's fully selected.
498	- Layers in front of the clip are left out, so a title on top doesn't hide the selection.
499	- The preview is black whenever the clip isn't on the frame, such as when the playhead is outside it.
500	- With no range turned on, the qualifier picks everything, so the whole frame is white. With **Invert** on as well, it's black.
501	
502	## The Selection tag
503	
504	A **Selection** tag shows in the preview's top-left corner while the switch is on. It sits beside the **Ungraded** tag, and moves into the corner when Show Ungraded is off. See [Preview tags](/timeline/preview/#preview-tags).
505	
506	## Which clip it shows
507	
508	Show Selection shows one clip at a time, the first selected adjustment clip.
509	
510	- Select a different adjustment clip and it moves to that one.
511	- Select something else, or nothing, so that no adjustment clip is selected, and it turns off.
512	
513	## Preview only
514	
515	Show Selection changes this window's preview and the [Preview Window](/timeline/preview-window/), and nothing else. An export and **Save Frame…** never see it.
516	
517	It isn't an edit, so it makes no undo step and the project doesn't change. It belongs to the window and isn't saved, so a new window starts with it off. See [Grade view tools are never saved](/color/show-ungraded/#grade-view-tools-are-never-saved).
518	
519	## Good to know
520	
521	- [Scopes](/color/scopes/) read the preview's frame, so while Show Selection is on they measure the grey picture, not the graded one.
522	- It can be on at the same time as [Show Ungraded](/color/show-ungraded/). The clips behind the adjustment clip then lose their grades, so the selection is worked out from their ungraded picture.
523	
524	## With an agent
525	
526	`render_frame` can draw this same grey picture for any frame. Pass an adjustment clip's id as `selection`. The tool works the same whether the View menu switch is on or off, and it leaves the switch alone. If the id isn't an adjustment clip in this project, the tool stops with an error naming `selection`. See [Check the picture: render_frame](/mcp/render-frame/#selection).
527	
528	## Related
529	
530	- [Qualifiers](/color/qualifiers/)
531	- [Pick from Canvas](/color/pick-from-canvas/)
532	- [Adjustment clips](/color/adjustment-clips/)

534	---
535	title: Adjustment clips
536	description: Grade everything behind a clip in one place, over a range, a selection or the whole timeline, and set how strongly the grade applies.
537	---
538	
539	import { Steps } from '@astrojs/starlight/components';
540	import AtAGlance from '@components/AtAGlance.astro';
541	import Shot from '@components/Shot.astro';
542	
543	An adjustment clip has no picture of its own. For as long as it lasts, it grades everything already drawn behind it, so one grade can cover a whole scene, or a graphic that has no Color tab of its own.
544	
545	<AtAGlance
546	  menu="Insert ▸ Adjustment Clip"
547	  where="Clip tab ▸ Color ▸ Adjustment"
548	  tools={['add_adjustment_clip', 'set_video', 'set_action_end']}
549	/>
550	
551	<Shot
552	  name="05c-clip-adjustment.window"
553	  alt="The editor with a rose clip named Adjustment selected on its own track, above a video clip on the Video track. The inspector shows only the Color and Clip sub-tabs. Color opens on the Adjustment section with Strength at 75%, then the Qualifier section, which reads off."
554	/>
555	
556	## What an adjustment clip is
557	
558	An adjustment clip grades every lower track and the canvas background. It never touches a track in front of it, so a title above it stays as it is.
559	
560	On the timeline it's a plain rose block with its name strip and action lane, and no filmstrip. It has no file behind it, so no media length holds it back. Trim or move it to change what it covers.
561	
562	## Insert an adjustment clip
563	
564	<Steps>
565	
566	1. Say what it should cover: set an [In–Out range](/timeline/in-out-range/), or select the clips. With neither, it covers the whole timeline.
567	
568	2. Choose **Insert ▸ Adjustment Clip**. It has no shortcut.
569	
570	3. Grade in the **Color** sub-tab, which is already open. The new clip is selected and the inspector shows **Clip ▸ Color**.
571	
572	</Steps>
573	
574	The whole thing is one undo step, **Add Adjustment Clip**. The menu item is greyed out while a nest is open, and when the timeline has nothing to cover.
575	
576	### Its span
577	
578	| What's set | What the new clip covers |
579	| --- | --- |
580	| An In–Out range | The range, even if clips are selected too |
581	| Selected clips, no range | From the first selected clip's start to the last one's end |
582	| Neither | The whole timeline |
583	
584	### Its track
585	
586	The new clip goes on the front track when that track has room for the whole span and isn't a matte track. Otherwise Frame Job adds a new front track named **Adjustment** and puts the clip there. A matte front track is never used, because an adjustment clip on one [does nothing](#confine-it-to-part-of-the-picture).
587	
588	A project holds up to 64 tracks, counting the tracks inside nests. If the clip needs a new track and there are none to spare, nothing is added.
589	
590	## The full grade
591	
592	An adjustment clip's **Color** sub-tab has the same grade a picture clip has, plus two sections of its own at the top. In order:
593	
594	| Section | What it does |
595	| --- | --- |
596	| **Adjustment** | [Strength](#strength), how much of the grade is applied |
597	| **Qualifier** | Narrows the grade to the pixels you pick. See [Qualifiers](/color/qualifiers/). |
598	| [Light](/color/light/) | Exposure and tone |
599	| [Color](/color/color-section/) | Brightness, contrast, saturation and hue |
600	| [Wheels](/color/wheels/) | Balance shadows, middle and highlights |
601	| [Curves](/color/curves/) | Master, RGB and [hue curves](/color/hue-curves/) |
602	| [Look](/color/looks/) | A built-in look or a [.cube LUT](/color/luts/) |
603	
604	**Adjustment** and **Qualifier** show only when every selected clip is an adjustment clip. Select one alongside a picture clip and you get the shared grade sections without those two.
605	
606	### No Picture tab
607	
608	An adjustment clip has nothing to place or crop, so it has no **Picture** sub-tab. Its sub-tabs are **Color** and **Clip**. **Picture** also disappears whenever any adjustment clip is part of the selection.
609	
610	Placement, crop, corners, shadow, reflection and the like can still arrive on one through [Paste Attributes](/editing/paste-attributes/). They're kept and have no effect.
611	
612	## Strength
613	
614	**Strength** sets how much of the grade is mixed over the picture behind the clip. At 100 % you see the full grade, and at 0 % you see the picture as it was.
615	
616	| Control | Range | Default |
617	| --- | --- | --- |
618	| **Strength** | 0 to 100 %, in whole percent, with presets at 0, 25, 50, 75 and 100 behind the field's chevron | 100 % |
619	
620	The section's header shows the current strength. Its **Reset** button returns to 100 %, as one undo step named **Adjustment**.
621	
622	## Fade the grade in or out
623	
624	An adjustment clip can't take a transition, so animate its **Strength** with an [action](/motion/actions/) instead. To fade a grade in:
625	
626	<Steps>
627	
628	1. Select the adjustment clip and set **Strength** to 0 %.
629	
630	2. Put the playhead where the fade should start and press <kbd>⌥⌘K</kbd> to [add an action](/motion/add-an-action/). It lasts 1 second, and you can [resize it](/motion/change-an-action/) afterwards.
631	
632	3. With the action selected, set **Strength** to 100 %. The grade ramps there from the Strength the clip has when the action starts.
633	
634	4. Press <kbd>Esc</kbd> to go back to editing the clip itself.
635	
636	</Steps>
637	
638	To fade a grade out, leave the clip's **Strength** where it is, add an action near the end of the clip and set **Strength** to 0 % inside it. See [Animate a grade](/color/animate-a-grade/).
639	
640	## Confine it to part of the picture
641	
642	An adjustment clip grades the whole frame behind it. There are two ways to narrow that:
643	
644	- **To an area:** put a [matte track](/canvas/matte-tracks/) directly in front of the adjustment clip's track. On a track cut by a matte, the clip grades only inside the matte. The matte cuts everything on that track, so keep other clips off it.
645	- **To a colour or brightness:** set a [qualifier](/color/qualifiers/). It picks pixels by hue, saturation and luma.
646	
647	The two work together. The grade reaches only the pixels both allow, mixed at the clip's Strength.
648	
649	The adjustment clip must not sit on the matte track itself. There it has no effect, and the inspector says "An adjustment clip on a matte track has no effect."
650	
651	## Grade a graphic
652	
653	[Graphics](/graphics/graphic-tab/) have no **Color** sub-tab, and neither do text, shapes or nests. To grade one, put an adjustment clip above it for the span you want. Select the clip first and **Insert ▸ Adjustment Clip** matches its span, unless an In–Out range is set. The adjustment clip grades every track behind it, so add a matte if other tracks show through.
654	
655	## Limits
656	
657	### No nests
658	
659	An adjustment clip can't go inside a nest. **Insert ▸ Adjustment Clip** is greyed out while one is open, Frame Job won't [nest](/editing/nests/) a selection that holds an adjustment clip, and pasting one into an open nest fails. Inside a nest it would grade the layers behind the nest clip as well as the nest's own.
660	
661	To grade a nest, put an adjustment clip above the nest clip on the timeline.
662	
663	### No transitions or overlaps
664	
665	An adjustment clip can't take a [transition](/motion/transitions/), and it can't overlap another clip on its track, because an overlap is a transition. Frame Job won't make the edit, so [fade its Strength](#fade-the-grade-in-or-out) instead. Two clips that only touch are fine.
666	
667	### No blur, sharpen, pixelate or blend modes
668	
669	These need pixels or a colour of the clip's own, and an adjustment clip has neither. If [Paste Attributes](/editing/paste-attributes/) would bring one onto an adjustment clip, nothing is pasted.
670	
671	The point [filters](/effects/filters/), **Sepia**, **Noir**, **Vignette** and **Invert**, do work, and apply to the picture behind it. An adjustment clip has no **Picture** sub-tab, so they reach it through Paste Attributes or an agent.
672	
673	## Good to know
674	
675	- A clip with no grade set changes nothing, and neither does a qualifier on its own. A qualifier narrows a grade, so there has to be one.
676	- **Clip ▸ Speed…**, **Clip ▸ Speed Ramp…** and **Clip ▸ Add Blurred Background** are dimmed for an adjustment clip, and its **Clip** sub-tab has no [Speed](/speed/speed-section/) section, because it has no source and no picture size. [Retime Range](/speed/retime-range/) still stretches or squeezes one inside its range.
677	
678	## With an agent
679	
680	`add_adjustment_clip` places a clip on the `track` and `at` the time you name, and it lasts 5 seconds unless you give a `duration`. It doesn't work out a span or a track as the menu does, so an agent can put one on a matte track, where it does nothing. It won't add one while a nest is open.
681	
682	`set_video` then grades it with everything the Color tab offers, and can also give it point filters directly. To an agent, Strength is the clip's `opacity`, from 0 to 1, and `set_action_end` animates it. A blur, sharpen or pixelate filter or a blend mode is an error, such as "clip 7 is an adjustment clip and cannot take the blur filter". See [Tools: adding clips](/mcp/tools-adding-clips/#add_adjustment_clip) and [Tools: picture and grade](/mcp/tools-set-video/#on-an-adjustment-clip).
683

693	title: "Animate a grade"
694	description: "Put a grade inside an action so it changes over time: what ramps, what switches at the end, how each control shows it, and how to take it back out."
695	---
696	
697	import { Steps } from '@astrojs/starlight/components';
698	import AtAGlance from '@components/AtAGlance.astro';
699	
700	Most grade settings can change over time. Put a change inside an [action](/motion/actions/) and a shot can warm up as the sun comes out, drain to black and white, or ease into a new contrast curve.
701	
702	<AtAGlance
703	  menu="Clip ▸ Add Action"
704	  keys="⌥⌘K"
705	  where={['Clip tab ▸ action lane', 'Clip tab ▸ Color']}
706	  tools={['add_action', 'set_action_end', 'set_video']}
707	/>
708	
709	## Grade inside an action
710	
711	<Steps>
712	
713	1. Select the clip and [add an action](/motion/add-an-action/), or [select one](/motion/select-an-action/) on its action lane.
714	
715	2. Open the **Clip** tab's **Color** sub-tab.
716	
717	3. Change a control. The change goes to the action's end state, and the value ramps there from where it stands when the action starts.
718	
719	4. Move the playhead through the action, or play it, to watch the grade travel.
720	
721	</Steps>
722	
723	Light, Color, Wheels, Curves and the look's **Amount** can all animate, and on an [adjustment clip](/color/adjustment-clips/) so can **Strength** and the [Qualifier](/color/qualifiers/).
724	
725	While the action is selected, every control shows the value at the action's end. When you're done, press <kbd>Esc</kbd> to go back to editing the clip itself. See [Set what an action animates to](/motion/edit-an-action/) for how an action's end state works in every tab.
726	
727	:::tip
728	An adjustment clip can't take a transition. To fade a grade in, set its **Strength** to 0 % on the clip, then add an action and raise **Strength** to 100 %.
729	:::
730	
731	## What ramps smoothly
732	
733	These move gradually from the start value to the end value, along the action's [easing curve](/motion/actions/#easing-curves):
734	
735	- every slider in **Light** and **Color**
736	- each wheel's colour push and master in **Wheels**
737	- the look's **Amount**
738	- **Strength** on an adjustment clip
739	- the Qualifier's numbers: **Centre**, **Width**, **Soft**, **Low**, **High** and **Blur**
740	
741	## Curves animate
742	
743	Curves in an action always animate, on all six channels, including **Hue** and **Sat**. An edit to a curve goes to the action's end even when you add or delete a point.
744	
745	| The two curves | How they animate |
746	| --- | --- |
747	| Same number of points | They ramp point by point |
748	| One is a straight line | The straight one lines up with the other curve's points, then they ramp point by point |
749	| Different numbers of points | Their values blend over the action, from the first curve's result to the second's |
750	
751	### Animate a curve back to neutral
752	
753	To have a curve straighten out over the action, write a straight curve to its end:
754	
755	- For one channel, right-click its cell in the picker and choose **Reset Red**, or whichever channel it is. The item is greyed out while that channel is already straight.
756	- For every channel, right-click the plot and choose **Set end value to default**.
757	
758	The section's **Reset** isn't there while an action is selected. See [Master and RGB curves](/color/curves/).
759	
760	## A look switches instead
761	
762	Turning a look on or off, or changing it, applies to the clip itself and not to the action, even with an action selected. A look tile, **None** and **Clip ▸ Look** all change the clip's own look, as one undo step called Look, and the change shows across the whole clip.
763	
764	**Amount** is what animates. To fade a look in, choose the look and set **Amount** to 0 % with no action selected, then select an action and raise **Amount**. The Amount row only shows once the clip has a look, so choose the look first.
765	
766	## Animate a qualifier
767	
768	A qualifier's numbers ramp, but a range itself can't fade in or out.
769	
770	### A qualifier range switches
771	
772	Ticking **Hue**, **Saturation** or **Luma** with an action selected turns that range on at the action's end. It has nothing to ramp from, so it stays off through the action and then appears whole, at the end values you set. **Invert** switches at the end too.
773	
774	If the clip has no qualifier at all when the action starts, the whole qualifier appears at the action's end, and its **Blur** doesn't ramp either.
775	
776	An action can't turn off a range the clip already has on. Unticking a box with an action selected only takes that range back out of the action. To turn a range off, press <kbd>Esc</kbd> and untick it on the clip.
777	
778	### A hue centre takes the short way
779	
780	An animated **Centre** goes the short way round the colour wheel, so 350° to 10° passes through 0° and never visits the greens and blues. Two centres exactly 180° apart have no short way, so the number moves straight from one to the other.
781	
782	## See what the action animates
783	
784	Row marks and the tab badge show what the selected action does to the grade.
785	
786	- **◆** in a row's gutter means the selected action animates that row. See [Read the row marks](/motion/edit-an-action/#read-the-row-marks) for all the marks.
787	- **◆N** on the **Color** sub-tab counts how many grade settings the action animates.
788	
789	The badge counts settings, not values. Each of these counts as one, however many values inside it change:
790	
791	- Light and Color, together, for all thirteen sliders
792	- Wheels
793	- Curves
794	- Look
795	- Qualifier
796	- Strength, on an adjustment clip
797	
798	The same grouping decides the marks. All thirteen Light and Color sliders show ◆ as soon as the action changes one of them, and every Qualifier row does as soon as the action changes any part of the qualifier. The Qualifier's range rows and **Invert** read "at end" whenever that happens, even for a range whose numbers are ramping.
799	
800	## Take a setting back out
801	
802	| To | Do this |
803	| --- | --- |
804	| Take a row out of the action | Hover over its ◆ and click the ×, or right-click the row and choose **Remove from action N** |
805	| Take a section out of the action | Choose **Clear** in the section's header |
806	| Make the row animate to its default | Right-click the row and choose **Set end value to default** |
807	| Put a row back to its default on the clip itself, with no action selected | Right-click the row and choose **Reset to default** |
808	
809	**Clear** takes the place of **Reset** in a grade section's header while an action is selected, and shows only when the action animates one of that section's rows.
810	
811	The default items are greyed out while the row already holds its default. Text fields and popups keep their own right-click menus, so right-click a row's label, its slider or its gutter. On **Wheels** and **Curves** the whole section is one row, so these items act on all of it.
812	
813	:::caution
814	Light and Color are one setting inside an action, so **Remove from action N** on any slider takes all thirteen out, and so does **Clear** on either section. To change one slider back, use **Set end value to default**, or type a new end value.
815	:::
816	
817	## How each control shows an action
818	
819	| Control | While the action animates it |
820	| --- | --- |
821	| Slider | The same marks as everywhere else in the inspector. See [See the value change as it plays](/motion/edit-an-action/#see-the-value-change-as-it-plays) |
822	| Wheel disc | A hollow square at the action's start value, the puck in the action colour, and a coral mark at the value under the playhead |
823	| Wheel strip | The strip fills in the action colour from the start value, the knob is in the action colour, and a coral tick marks the playhead's value |
824	| Curve plot | The action's start curve is dashed, and the edited curve and its points are in the action colour |
825	| Qualifier strip | The band is outlined and its knobs are drawn in the action colour |
826	
827	The coral marks show only when the playhead is on the clip and the value there differs from the end value. A qualifier's hue band that wraps past 0° gets its knobs in the action colour but no outline. The three wheels are one row, so all three discs and strips count as animated as soon as the action changes any one of them.
828	
829	## With an agent
830	
831	An agent uses `add_action`, then `set_action_end` with the end values in its `video` group: `color`, `wheels`, `curves`, `look.amount`, and on an adjustment clip `qualifier` and `opacity`, which is **Strength**. It changes the clip's own look with `set_video`. It can do one thing the Color tab can't: name a different look in an action's end. A look or LUT that differs between the start and the end switches at the action's end, **Amount** included. **Amount** ramps only while the look stays the same. See [Tools: animation](/mcp/tools-animation/#set_action_end).

20	  alt="The Qualifier section of the Color tab, with Hue ticked at Centre 25°, Width 30° and Soft 15°, Saturation ticked at Low 0.15, High 1.00 and Soft 0.05, Luma unticked, and the Pick from Canvas button beside a ticked Show Selection."

22	
23	## Pick a colour
24	
25	<Steps>
26	
27	1. Select the [adjustment clip](/color/adjustment-clips/), and move the playhead to a frame that shows the colour. The **Qualifier** section only appears while every selected clip is an adjustment clip. For any other selection the button beeps and no pick starts.
28	
29	2. In the [Color tab](/color/color-tab/), open the **Qualifier** section and press **Pick from Canvas**. The pointer becomes a crosshair over the preview, and a hint reads "Click to pick the colour to qualify · Esc to cancel".
30	
31	3. Click the colour in the preview.
32	
33	</Steps>
34	
35	The ranges move to that colour, and the pick ends. It's one undo step, named Qualifier.
36	
37	Frame Job reads the colour from the picture behind the adjustment clip, at the playhead. The clip's own grade and every layer in front of it are left out. So the colour you get is the one the qualifier will really test, even after your grade has changed how it looks, and clicking a title on top samples what's underneath it.
38	
39	Turn on [Show Selection](/color/show-selection/) to check what the pick caught.
40	
41	## What a pick sets
42	
43	| Range | If it was off | If it was on |
44	| --- | --- | --- |
45	| **Hue** | Turns on, centred on the colour, 30° wide with 15° softness. | Moves its centre to the colour. |
46	| **Saturation** | Turns on, centred on the colour's saturation, 0.3 wide with softness 0.1. | Moves to centre on the colour's saturation. |
47	| **Luma** | Stays off. | Moves to centre on the colour's brightness. |
48	
49	A range that was already on keeps its width and softness, so you can set how wide you want a range and then pick again to move it. **Invert** and **Blur** don't change.
50	
51	If you click a near-grey, there's no real hue to aim at, so **Hue** turns off. A near-grey here is a colour whose strongest and weakest channels are less than 0.06 apart, on a scale of 0 to 1. **Saturation** still turns on and centres, which is how you pick the greys in a picture.
52	
53	**Saturation** and **Luma** stay inside 0 to 1. A range that would cross either end is shifted back inside at its full width, so it's no longer centred on the colour, but the colour stays inside it.
54	
55	## Pick inside an action
56	
57	With an [action](/motion/select-an-action/) selected, the picked ranges go to the action's end state instead of the clip, as any qualifier control does. The width and softness a range keeps are the ones the section is showing. Clicking a near-grey takes **Hue** out of the end state rather than turning it off, so if the clip itself has **Hue** on, it stays on. See [Animate a grade](/color/animate-a-grade/).
58	
59	## Cancel a pick
60	
61	Press <kbd>Esc</kbd>, or press **Pick from Canvas** again. Changing the selection cancels the pick too. Nothing in the qualifier changes.
62	
63	A click in the area around the picture beeps and the pick stays on, so you can click again.
64	
65	## Good to know
66	
67	- Only one tool that waits for you on the preview can be on at a time. Starting Pick from Canvas cancels any other, such as the chroma key's eyedropper or a [Zoom to Region](/motion/zoom-to-region/) drag, and starting one of those cancels a pick.
68	- If the playhead isn't on the adjustment clip, no layers are left out, so you sample the frame as it's drawn.
69	- [Show Ungraded](/color/show-ungraded/) and [Show Selection](/color/show-selection/) don't change what you sample. A pick reads the real picture, whatever the preview is showing.
70	- With several adjustment clips selected, Frame Job samples behind the first and writes the same ranges to all of them.
71	- In an HDR (HLG) project, a pick reads the HLG values, which are what the qualifier tests.
72	- If the selection changes while Frame Job is sampling, it beeps and changes nothing.
73	
74	## With an agent
75	
76	No agent tool clicks the canvas. An agent writes the ranges itself with `set_video`, or with `set_action_end` for an action's end state. See [Tools: picture and grade](/mcp/tools-set-video/#qualifier).

86	title: "Scopes"
87	description: "Open the Scopes panel beside the preview to measure the picture while you grade, with two slots that each show a waveform, parade, vectorscope or histogram."
88	---
89	
90	import AtAGlance from '@components/AtAGlance.astro';
91	import Shot from '@components/Shot.astro';
92	
93	Scopes measure the picture while you grade, so you're not relying on your eyes or your display. The panel sits beside the preview and shows two scopes at once.
94	
95	<AtAGlance menu="View ▸ Scopes" keys="⌃⌘W" tools="render_frame" />
96	
97	<Shot
98	  name="04b-preview-scopes.preview"
99	  alt="The preview with the Scopes panel on its right. The top slot shows a Waveform with red clip marks and the readouts Highlights clipped 1.9 % and Shadows clipped 52.7 %. The bottom slot shows a Vectorscope with its six colour targets and 1×, 2× and 4× zoom cells. Both slots are captioned Rec. 709 · encoded."
100	/>
101	
102	## Open the scopes
103	
104	Press <kbd>⌃⌘W</kbd>, or choose **View ▸ Scopes**. Do the same again to close the panel. The menu item has a checkmark while it's open, and it's always available.
105	
106	The panel is a fixed column 248 pt wide, the full height of the preview pane, between the picture and the inspector. The picture shrinks to fit what's left, and takes the whole pane back when the panel closes. If the [Loudness Meter](/audio/loudness-meter/) is on too, its column sits between the picture and the scopes.
107	
108	The panel is off in every new window. Your scope choices and zooms last while the window is open, even if you close and reopen the panel, and they aren't saved.
109	
110	## Choose a scope for each slot
111	
112	The panel has two slots, one above the other. Each has a popup at its top left that picks one of four scopes. A new window opens on **Waveform** over **Vectorscope**.
113	
114	| Scope | What it shows |
115	| --- | --- |
116	| [Waveform](/color/waveform-and-parade/#read-the-waveform) | Brightness across the frame, left to right. |
117	| [Parade](/color/waveform-and-parade/#read-the-rgb-parade) | Red, green and blue as three waveforms side by side. |
118	| [Vectorscope](/color/vectorscope/) | Hue and saturation, with colour targets and the skin line. |
119	| [Histogram](/color/histogram/) | How many pixels sit at each level, per colour. |
120	
121	You can put the same scope in both slots. Each slot keeps its own vectorscope zoom, so two vectorscopes can show the picture at different zooms.
122	
123	## Read a slot's caption
124	
125	A faint caption at each slot's top right says what the scope is reading.
126	
127	| Project | Waveform and Parade | Vectorscope and Histogram |
128	| --- | --- | --- |
129	| SDR | Rec. 709 · encoded | Rec. 709 · encoded |
130	| HDR (HLG) | HLG · cd/m² | Rec. 2100 HLG |
131	
132	"Encoded" means the scope reads the picture's stored values, not the light they stand for. An HDR project also changes the scales and targets. See [Scopes in an HDR project](/hdr/hdr-scopes/).
133	
134	## When the pane is short
135	
136	Waveform and Parade want a height of 200 pt, Vectorscope a square of 224 pt and Histogram 140 pt. If the preview pane can't hold both slots at those sizes, they shrink together by the same proportion, and a vectorscope stays square and centred.
137	
138	Below a pane height of 360 pt, only the top slot shows. The bottom slot comes back, with its pick, when there's room again.
139	
140	## What the scopes measure
141	
142	The scopes measure the frames the preview draws. They follow the picture live while it plays, jumping to the newest frame if they fall behind, and update after each edit while it's paused. Until a frame has been measured, a slot is empty and its readouts show "—". The scopes only run while the panel is open, so they cost nothing when it's closed.
143	
144	They read the whole frame, so the project's background counts as part of the picture. A black background beside a smaller clip shows up as shadows at level 0.
145	
146	Because they read the preview's frame, they follow what the preview is showing:
147	
148	- With [Show Ungraded](/color/show-ungraded/) on, they measure the ungraded picture. In an HDR project they keep their HLG reading.
149	- With [Show Selection](/color/show-selection/) on, they measure the grey selection picture.
150	- With [Show SDR Version](/hdr/show-sdr-version/) on in an HDR (HLG) project, they measure the SDR picture exactly as in an SDR project, and switch to the Rec. 709 caption and targets.
151	
152	## With an agent
153	
154	No agent tool drives the panel. Instead, `render_frame` measures any of the four scopes on any frame, counting exactly as the panel does. Pass `waveform`, `parade`, `vectorscope` or `histogram` as true, and `vectorscope_zoom` as 1, 2 or 4 with a vectorscope. The tool's reply gives the figures in words, such as the clipping percentages, and a JSON file next to the image holds the counts. If the measurement can't run, the frame is still written and the tool says the scopes couldn't be measured. See [Check the picture: render_frame](/mcp/render-frame/#measure-the-frame).

165	title: "Histogram"
166	description: "See how a frame's tones are spread from black to white, and read how much of the picture is clipped at each end."
167	---
168	
169	import AtAGlance from '@components/AtAGlance.astro';
170	
171	The histogram shows how a frame's tones are spread: how much of the picture is dark, how much is bright, and whether either end has run out of room. Use it to judge exposure and contrast, and to catch clipping while you grade.
172	
173	<AtAGlance
174	  menu="View ▸ Scopes"
175	  keys="⌃⌘W"
176	  where="The Scopes panel ▸ a slot's popup ▸ Histogram"
177	  tools="render_frame"
178	/>
179	
180	## Open the histogram
181	
182	Choose **View ▸ Scopes**, then pick **Histogram** from a slot's popup. Neither slot opens on it, because a new window starts with **Waveform** over **Vectorscope**. The choice lasts while the window is open. See [Scopes](/color/scopes/) for the panel itself.
183	
184	## Read the histogram
185	
186	Levels run from 0 on the left to 255 on the right, so black is at the left edge and white is at the right. The height at each level is how many pixels sit there.
187	
188	Red, green and blue are drawn as translucent tinted fills, and luma, the picture's brightness, is a white line on top.
189	
190	| What you see | What it tells you |
191	| --- | --- |
192	| A pile against the left edge | Shadows are crushed to black |
193	| A pile against the right edge | Highlights are clipped to white |
194	| Empty space at both ends | A flat picture, with room to add contrast in [Light](/color/light/) or [Curves](/color/curves/) |
195	| One colour's fill sitting to the side of the others | That channel is brighter or darker overall, which often means a colour cast |
196	
197	Heights are on a logarithmic scale, so a small count still shows up beside a big one, and a peak twice as tall holds far more than twice the pixels. All four share one scale, set by the tallest count in any of them, so you can compare them directly.
198	
199	## Clipping readouts
200	
201	Two readouts sit below the histogram:
202	
203	- **Highlights clipped** is the share of the frame at the very top level, 255.
204	- **Shadows clipped** is the share at the very bottom level, 0.
205	
206	They read like "Highlights clipped 1.9 %", to one decimal place, and show "—" until a frame has been measured. The [Waveform](/color/waveform-and-parade/) shows the same two figures.
207	
208	Both are measured on luma, so read them with these in mind:
209	
210	- A single colour channel can clip while luma doesn't. Watch the fills at the right edge, or use the [Parade](/color/waveform-and-parade/), to catch that.
211	- They count the whole frame. Black canvas around a smaller picture, or letterbox bars, counts towards **Shadows clipped**.
212	
213	## Good to know
214	
215	- The histogram measures the frame the preview composes, so it follows playback, your edits and [Show Ungraded](/color/show-ungraded/). It changes nothing in the project or in an export.
216	- The slot's caption says what the scope reads: "Rec. 709 · encoded", the picture's own encoded values. In an HDR (HLG) project it reads "Rec. 2100 HLG", and luma is worked out for that colour space. With **Show SDR Version** on, the scope reads that SDR picture as it would in an SDR project. See [Scopes in an HDR project](/hdr/hdr-scopes/).
217	- The histogram is 140 pt tall. If the preview pane is too short for both slots, it shrinks with them. Under 360 pt tall, only the top slot shows.
218	
219	## With an agent
220	
221	`render_frame` measures a frame's histogram as numbers when an agent passes `histogram: true`, which is off by default. The reply says what share of the frame clips high and low by luma. The counts for red, green, blue and luma at each of the 256 levels, and both percentages, go to a `.histogram.json` file beside the image. See [Check the picture: render_frame](/mcp/render-frame/#waveform-parade-and-histogram).

241	  menu="View ▸ Scopes"

248	  name="04b-preview-scopes.preview"
249	  alt="The Waveform in the top slot of the Scopes panel beside the preview: a dark panel labelled 0, 50 and 100 at its left, with a white trace, red marks along its top and bottom edges, and under it the readouts Highlights clipped 1.9 % and Shadows clipped 52.7 %."
250	/>
251	
252	To see them, press <kbd>⌃⌘W</kbd> to open the [Scopes](/color/scopes/) panel, then choose **Waveform** or **Parade** from a slot's popup. A new window's top slot is already on **Waveform**. Each takes 200 pt of height when the pane has room, and [shrinks to fit](/color/scopes/#when-the-pane-is-short) when it doesn't.
253	
254	In an HDR project they read differently, and [Scopes in an HDR project](/hdr/hdr-scopes/) has the scale.
255	
256	## Read the waveform
257	
258	The Waveform plots the picture's luma (Y′, its brightness). Left to right in the scope is left to right across the frame, and height is brightness, with black at the bottom and white at the top. So a bright window on the left of the shot shows as a high patch on the left of the scope.
259	
260	Lines mark 0, 25, 50, 75 and 100 %, with 0, 50 and 100 labelled at the left. The trace is white on a near-black background in both light and dark appearance. The brighter a point in the trace, the more pixels sit there, on a log scale, so a level only a few pixels reach still shows.
261	
262	## Read the RGB parade
263	
264	The Parade shows red, green and blue as three waveforms side by side, in that order, each tinted its own colour. Each one works like the Waveform, with the same lines and the whole width of the frame.
265	
266	Use it to see a colour cast. Something that should be neutral grey sits at the same height in all three, and a channel sitting higher or lower is pulling the picture toward or away from that colour. **Temperature** and **Tint** in [Light](/color/light/), and the [wheels](/color/wheels/), are the usual ways to bring them back in line.
267	
268	## Find clipping
269	
270	A pixel clips high at the top level, where an 8-bit file would write 255, and low at the bottom level, where it would write 0. Detail at those levels has gone flat.
271	
272	**Clip marks** are red marks on the top and bottom edges of the scope. A mark sits over every column where at least 0.5 % of the pixels clip, on the top edge for highlights and the bottom edge for shadows, so you can see where in the frame it's happening. The Parade marks each channel on its own, so one channel can clip when the others don't.
273	
274	**Readouts** under the Waveform give the share of the whole frame, for example **Highlights clipped 1.9 %** and **Shadows clipped 52.7 %**. They show "—" until a frame has been measured. The [Histogram](/color/histogram/) has the same two readouts. The Parade and the Vectorscope have none.
275	
276	The readouts count everything in the frame. A black background around a smaller clip counts as clipped shadows, so a high figure may not be a problem with your footage. To bring highlights down, try **Exposure** or **Highlights** in [Light](/color/light/).
277	
278	## With an agent
279	
280	`render_frame` measures a frame's Waveform or Parade without the panel. Pass `waveform` or `parade` as true. Both are false by default. The tool's reply says what share of pixels clips high and low, and for the Parade it gives that for each channel, which the panel doesn't show as a number.
281	
282	A JSON file next to the image holds the raw counts, in 256 × 256 bins, with the clip marks and the clipping figures. It's named `<image path>.waveform.json` or `<image path>.parade.json`, and the Parade's holds red, green and blue separately. See [Check the picture: render_frame](/mcp/render-frame/#waveform-parade-and-histogram).

313	
314	## Open the vectorscope
315	
316	Choose **View ▸ Scopes**. In a new window the panel starts with **Waveform** on top and **Vectorscope** below. If a slot shows something else, pick **Vectorscope** from its popup. Both slots can show it, each at its own zoom. See [Scopes](/color/scopes/) for the panel itself.
317	
318	## Read the trace
319	
320	Every pixel in the frame lands somewhere on the near-black square, and the white trace is all of them together.
321	
322	- **The centre is no colour.** Greys, black and white all sit on the faint cross.
323	- **Distance from the centre is strength.** A pale colour stays close in, and a saturated one reaches out towards the edge.
324	- **Direction is hue.** The [targets](#the-targets) show which way each colour lies.
325	- **Brightness is how many pixels are there.** The scale is logarithmic, so a small patch of colour still shows up beside a large one.
326	
327	The two axes are the colour-difference signals: Cb runs across and Cr runs up. The scope draws no circles and has no readouts, so the targets and the skin line are your only references.
328	
329	A picture with no colour cast keeps its neutral areas on the cross. If something that should be grey sits to one side of it, the picture leans the way the trace leans. [Zoom in](#zoom-in-on-a-low-saturation-picture) to see a small cast.
330	
331	## The targets
332	
333	Six boxes mark where 75 % colour bars land, so you can tell which way a colour lies and how strong it is. Each label sits outside its box, away from the centre.
334	
335	| Label | Colour | Where it sits |
336	| --- | --- | --- |
337	| R | Red | Up, a little left |
338	| Mg | Magenta | Up and right |
339	| B | Blue | Right, a little down |
340	| Cy | Cyan | Down, a little right |
341	| G | Green | Down and left |
342	| Yl | Yellow | Left, a little up |
343	
344	## The skin line
345	
346	The line running out from the centre, up and to the left, marks where skin tones fall. It's drawn at the hue of a standard light-skin reference colour, 123.3° anticlockwise from the right.
347	
348	Skin has a similar hue across complexions, and mostly differs in brightness and strength. If the trace from a face sits well to one side of the line, the picture has a cast.
349	
350	## Zoom in on a low-saturation picture
351	
352	The **1×**, **2×** and **4×** cells in the scope's bottom-right corner zoom in around the centre, to show small casts in a picture with little colour in it. Click a cell to choose it. The filled cell is the current zoom.
353	
354	Frame Job counts the pixels again at each zoom instead of enlarging the picture of the trace, so a magnified trace stays sharp.
355	
356	At 2× and 4×, a pixel too strong to fit on the square is left off, and it isn't piled up against the edge. At 1× everything fits.
357	
358	All six targets are too far out to fit at 2× and 4×. Each one becomes a 6 pt tick on the rim that points towards it, with its label inside the rim.
359	
360	Each slot keeps its own zoom when you pick another scope and come back, and when you hide the panel and show it again. A zoom lasts while the window is open. It isn't saved, and every slot starts at 1× in a new window. A cell works on the first click, even when its window isn't the active one.
361	
362	## Good to know
363	
364	- The scope measures the frame the preview composes, so it follows playback, your edits and [Show Ungraded](/color/show-ungraded/). It changes nothing in the project or in an export.
365	- The slot's caption says what the scope reads: "Rec. 709 · encoded", the picture's own encoded values.
366	- In an HDR (HLG) project the caption reads "Rec. 2100 HLG", and the targets and the skin line are redrawn for that colour space, with the skin line at 139.9°. With **Show SDR Version** on, the scope reads that SDR picture as it would in an SDR project. See [Scopes in an HDR project](/hdr/hdr-scopes/).
367	- The scope is a 224 pt square. If the preview pane is too short for both slots, it shrinks with them and stays square. Under 360 pt tall, only the top slot shows.
368	
369	## With an agent
370	
371	`render_frame` measures a frame's vectorscope as numbers when an agent passes `vectorscope: true`, which is off by default. `vectorscope_zoom` chooses 1, 2 or 4, and is 1 unless set. The reply says what share of the frame is neutral and, at 2 and 4, what share lies off the plot. The counts, the targets and the skin line's angle go to a `.vectorscope.json` file beside the image. None of this changes a slot's zoom in the panel. See [Check the picture: render_frame](/mcp/render-frame/#vectorscope-and-vectorscope_zoom).

402	## The Ungraded tag
403	
404	An **Ungraded** tag shows in the preview's top-left corner while the switch is on, so you can't mistake the plain picture for your grade. See [Preview tags](/timeline/preview/#preview-tags).
405	
406	## What it leaves on
407	
408	Show Ungraded only takes away the grade. These aren't part of the grade, so they stay on:
409	
410	- A [camera-log conversion](/hdr/camera-log/) on the media. It's how the file is read, so turning it off wouldn't give you the true source.
411	- [Filters](/effects/filters/).
412	- The [chroma key](/effects/chroma-key/).
413	- Placement, and everything else about a clip, such as its opacity and blend mode.
414	
415	## Grade view tools are never saved
416	
417	Show Ungraded, [Show Selection](/color/show-selection/) and the [scopes](/color/scopes/) only change how this window shows the picture. Each belongs to the window, each is off in a new window, and nothing about them is saved.
418	
419	None of them reaches an export or **Save Frame…**, which always use the graded picture. The thumbnails in the [Look](/color/looks/) gallery ignore Show Ungraded too.
420	
421	## With an agent
422	
423	Pass `ungraded: true` to `render_frame` to draw a frame as if no clip were graded. It's false by default, and the tool's reply says the frame has every grade removed. The tool works the same whether the View menu switch is on or off, and it leaves the switch alone. See [Check the picture: render_frame](/mcp/render-frame/#ungraded).
424	
425	## Related
426	
427	- [Scopes](/color/scopes/)
428	- [Show Selection](/color/show-selection/)
429	- [The Color tab](/color/color-tab/)
430	- [Show SDR Version](/hdr/show-sdr-version/)
431	---
432	title: "Copy a grade"
433	description: "Give other clips the grade you built on one clip, what comes with it, how LUTs and qualifiers travel, and what stops a paste."
434	---
435	
436	import { Steps } from '@astrojs/starlight/components';
437	import AtAGlance from '@components/AtAGlance.astro';
438	
439	When one clip looks right, Paste Attributes gives its grade to any number of other clips in one undo step. This page covers what that means for a grade. [Paste Attributes](/editing/paste-attributes/) covers the command in full.
440	
441	<AtAGlance
442	  menu="Edit ▸ Paste Attributes"
443	  keys={['⌘C', '⌥⌘V']}
444	  tools={['paste_attributes', 'paste']}
445	/>
446	
447	## Copy a grade with Paste Attributes
448	
449	<Steps>
450	
451	1. Select the graded clip and press <kbd>⌘C</kbd>.
452	
453	2. Select the clips that should take the grade.
454	
455	3. Press <kbd>⌥⌘V</kbd>, or choose **Edit ▸ Paste Attributes**.
456	
457	</Steps>
458	
459	The copied clip's video settings replace each selected clip's, as one undo step called Paste Attributes. If nothing would change, Frame Job beeps.
460	
461	## What comes with the grade
462	
463	There's no way to paste the grade alone, because it travels with the rest of the clip's picture settings:
464	
465	- Light, Color, Wheels, Curves, and the look with its **Amount**
466	- filters
467	- everything else about the picture, including position and scale
468	- the audio settings too, where the copied clip has sound and the target can take them
469	
470	A clip's place, speed, actions, transitions, name and label never come across.
471	
472	:::caution
473	Position and scale come with the grade. Pasting onto a clip you've already placed moves it to where the copied clip sits. To share a grade without touching placement, put an [adjustment clip](/color/adjustment-clips/) above the clips instead.
474	:::
475	
476	The paste replaces, it doesn't merge, so anything the target had that the copied clip didn't is gone. A grade that lives in an [action](/color/animate-a-grade/) doesn't travel either, because actions stay behind. The target takes the copied clip's own values, not its animation.
477	
478	## LUTs travel with a paste
479	
480	A look that uses an imported [`.cube` LUT](/color/luts/) keeps working when you paste it into another project, with Paste Attributes or with **Edit ▸ Paste**. The LUT arrives in that project's media along with the clip, and if the project already has the same file, the paste uses that one.
481	
482	A pasted look never lands on the wrong file. If what's being pasted doesn't carry the LUT, the clip gets no look.
483	
484	## A qualifier between clips
485	
486	A [qualifier](/color/qualifiers/) belongs to an adjustment clip, so what happens to it depends on the clips at both ends of the paste.
487	
488	| Pasting | The qualifier |
489	| --- | --- |
490	| Onto a picture clip | Is dropped |
491	| From a picture clip onto an adjustment clip | Stays as the adjustment clip had it |
492	| From one adjustment clip onto another | Is copied |
493	
494	## When a paste stops
495	
496	An adjustment clip has no picture of its own, so some settings can't land on it. If the copied clip has a blur, sharpen or pixelate filter, or a blend mode, pasting onto an adjustment clip shows an error naming the clip and the setting, and nothing changes on any selected clip.
497	
498	Sepia, noir, vignette and invert filters paste onto an adjustment clip without trouble.
499	
500	To get past it, take the setting off the copied clip and copy it again, or leave the adjustment clip out of the selection. [When a paste stops](/editing/paste-attributes/#when-a-paste-stops) has the full list, for every kind of clip.
501	
502	## With an agent
503	
504	The menu item always copies each of the picture, sound, text and shape groups both clips have. An agent can list the ones it wants in `paste_attributes`'s `groups`, out of `video`, `audio`, `text`, `shape` and `graphic`, so `["video"]` brings the picture settings and leaves the sound alone. The grade is still part of `video`, so to set a grade and nothing else, an agent uses `set_video`. See [Tools: copying and nesting](/mcp/tools-copy-and-nest/#paste_attributes).
505	
506	## Related
507	
508	- [Paste Attributes](/editing/paste-attributes/)
509	- [Copy, cut and paste](/editing/copy-and-paste/)
510	- [Animate a grade](/color/animate-a-grade/)
511	- [Adjustment clips](/color/adjustment-clips/)
512	- [.cube LUTs](/color/luts/)
513	- [Qualifiers](/color/qualifiers/)
